brief_summary:
This is a prospective, single-arm study in patients with locally advanced or metastatic pancreatic cancer that cannot be treated with surgery. The study is planned to enroll 42 patients. All patients will receive nimotuzumab combined with the NALIRIFOX chemotherapy regimen as first-line treatment.

Nimotuzumab is a targeted antibody against EGFR. NALIRIFOX is a standard first-line chemotherapy regimen for advanced pancreatic cancer and includes liposomal irinotecan, oxaliplatin, leucovorin, and 5-FU. Nimotuzumab 400 mg will be given intravenously on Day 1 every 2 weeks. The NALIRIFOX regimen will also be given every 2 weeks. Treatment will continue until the cancer grows or the side effects become unacceptable.

The main purpose of this study is to find out how long patients live without their cancer getting worse (progression-free survival, PFS). The study will also look at overall survival, tumor response rate, disease control rate, time to progression, and safety, especially serious side effects.

Patients will be followed closely during treatment. Imaging tests will be done every 8 weeks to check the cancer. After treatment ends, patients will be followed for survival for up to 24 months after the last patient is enrolled.
interventions: imotuzumab combined with the NALIRIFOX chemotherapy
title: A Single-Arm Study of Nimotuzumab Combined With NALIRIFOX as First-Line Treatment for Pancreatic Cancer

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to improve hypertensive patients' systolic blood pressure (SBP) through increased application of MI micro-skills by mitigating known implementation barriers through a structured reinforcement programme delivered via digital nudges to Primary Care Healthcare Professionals (HCPs).

Secondary goals include examining implementation outcome measures through validated instruments, and participants' confidence levels in the application of MI that will be measured by a pre-and-post intervention short survey.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* In primary care HCPs previously trained in MI, does undergoing a structured reinforcement program on MI micro-skills, compared to no reinforcement, result in lower patient SBP within 17 weeks of intervention commencement?
* How did intervention group participants' anticipated acceptability, appropriateness and feasibility compare with their perceptions after experiencing the intervention?
* Does confidence in the application of motivational interviewing (MI) change following the intervention among healthcare professionals in the intervention group?

Researchers will compare HCPs assigned to the intervention group with those assigned to the control group to determine whether structured reinforcement improves MI practice and is associated with differences in patient blood pressure outcomes.

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned to either an intervention group or a control group.
* Complete electronic questionnaires at baseline and after the intervention period.
* If assigned to the intervention group, participate in a community of practice through the Teams channel and receive a structured reinforcement programme consisting of digital nudges delivered through a Microsoft Teams channel over 17 weeks.
* The digital nudges consist of bite-sized infographic-based learning materials focused on MI micro-skills and key principles.

Patient blood pressure data from eligible patients with hypertension managed by participating healthcare professionals will be extracted from routine clinical records in a de-identified manner for analysis.
interventions: Digital Nudges for Motivational Interviewing (MI) Micro-Skills Reinforcement
primary_outcomes: Change From Baseline in Systolic Blood Pressure
title: Digital Reinforcement of Motivational Interviewing Micro-Skills Among Primary Care Healthcare Professionals

brief_summary: Kidney transplant recipients frequently experience reduced physical function, muscle weakness, low levels of physical activity, and an increased risk of cardiovascular and metabolic complications, despite improvements in survival and quality of life following transplantation. Therapeutic exercise has been shown to improve cardiorespiratory fitness, muscle strength, and physical function in this population. However, access to supervised rehabilitation programmes after transplantation remains limited. Online exercise programmes may provide an accessible and feasible alternative, particularly for patients who face geographical or logistical barriers to attending supervised in-person sessions.
primary_outcomes: Adherence to the Online Exercise Programme
Number of Adverse Events During the Exercise Programme

brief_summary:
The present study aims to determine whether a personalized digital psychoeducation intervention (active intervention group) is more effective than self-monitoring of one's mood (control group) in reducing emotion regulation difficulties, depression, anxiety, and stress symptoms in at-risk youths exposed to adverse childhood experiences (ACEs).

We hypothesized that the active intervention group will be associated with less severe emotion regulation difficulties, depression, anxiety, and stress symptoms than the control group at post-intervention and 3-month follow-up. This study will recruit a total of N = 140 youths (age 15 to 35 years) with ACEs and randomized into either the active intervention group (n = 70) or the control group (n = 70). Participants will complete study measures at baseline, post-intervention, and at 3-month follow-up. The study team has expertise in youth mental health. This study is feasible and will be completed within 4 years. Our findings will support the development and implementation of an efficacious, cost-effective, personalized and scalable intervention to reduce poor mental health and prevent the onset of mental disorders among at-risk youths. Our intervention has significant potential to improve population health, quality of life, functioning, morbidity, and mortality, as well as alleviate the healthcare burden associated with ACEs.
interventions: Personalized digital psychoeducation intervention on emotion regulation
primary_outcomes: Depression, Anxiety, and Stress as Assessed by DASS-21
Global Emotion Dysregulation as Assessed by the DERS-SF
Ecological Assessment of Momentary Emotion Dysregulation

title: Preventive and Personalized Digital Emotion Regulation Skills Intervention to Reduce Depression and Anxiety in Youths With Adverse Childhood Experiences

brief_summary: This study aims to evaluate and compare the measurement reliability, total time cost (preparation, acquisition, post-processing), and participant comfort of conventional limb volume measurement methods (water displacement volumetry, tape-based circumference measurement) against modern digital techniques (LiDAR-based mobile scanning, stereophotogrammetric 3D optical scanning) in the upper extremity. The evaluation will be conducted on both healthy adults and patients diagnosed with upper extremity lymphedema. Additionally, the impact of assessor experience on digital data post-processing and the sensitivity of the methods to detect small localized volume increases using a simulated edema model (50 mL) will be investigated.
title: Comparison of Reliability, Time Cost, and Participant Comfort of Lymphedema Assessments in Upper Extremity

brief_summary:
This study is designed as a prospective, observational research project conducted in collaboration between the Department of Periodontology at the Faculty of Dentistry and the Division of Gastroenterology at the Faculty of Medicine, Recep Tayyip Erdoğan University (RTEÜ). The study will include volunteers aged 18-65 who have a confirmed diagnosis of MASLD (metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease) and have been referred from the Gastroenterology Clinic to the Periodontology Clinic. All participants will be informed about the study, and written informed consent will be obtained.

For all natural teeth present in the mouths of the patients in the study groups, measurements of probing pocket depth, clinical attachment loss, plaque index, gingival index, and bleeding index will be recorded, and gingival crevicular fluid (GCF) samples will be collected. GCF samples will be obtained from the four sites with the deepest periodontal pockets using specially prepared paper strips. Subsequently, nursing staff at the RTEÜ Faculty of Dentistry will collect 5 ml of venous blood from each patient-following a 15-20 minute rest period-between 08:00 and 10:00 AM. The blood samples will be centrifuged (4000 rpm for 10 minutes) and stored at -80°C at the faculty until the day of analysis. The collection of serum and GCF samples from the study participants involves non-invasive procedures that do not require anesthesia.

Levels of 25(OH)D3 in the GCF and serum samples will be determined using the ELISA method. Total antioxidant capacity (TAC) and total oxidant capacity (TOC) will be measured via colorimetric methods, and the oxidative stress index (OSI) will be calculated using the TOC/TAC ratio. RANKL and OPG levels will be analyzed exclusively in serum samples using the ELISA method.
interventions: collection of GCF and serum samples
title: Periodontal Status and Biomarkers in MASLD

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn how well different preoxygenation targets reflect the actual amount of oxygen in the blood in adults having planned surgery under general anesthesia. Preoxygenation means breathing pure oxygen through a face mask before going to sleep, so that the body has an oxygen reserve while the breathing tube is placed.

Doctors usually decide that preoxygenation is adequate either after 3 minutes of breathing oxygen or when the oxygen level in exhaled air (end-tidal oxygen, EtO2) reaches 90% or more. A newer finger sensor measures the Oxygen Reserve Index (ORI), a noninvasive number that may show oxygen reserve continuously. However, it is not clear how closely these targets match the oxygen level measured directly in arterial blood (PaO2).

The main questions this study aims to answer are whether the arterial oxygen level (PaO2) differs when ORI reaches 0.45, when EtO2 reaches 90%, and at the 3rd minute of preoxygenation, and whether an ORI value of 0.45 or higher reflects an adequate arterial oxygen reserve.

Participants who already need an arterial line for their surgery will breathe 100% oxygen through a tight-fitting face mask for up to 5 minutes before anesthesia induction. Small blood samples will be taken from the existing arterial line at each target point. No additional invasive procedure will be done for the study.
conditions: Preoxygenation Adequacy Assessed by Oxygen Reserve Index, End-tidal Oxygen and Arterial Blood Gas
primary_outcomes: Arterial Partial Pressure of Oxygen (PaO2) at Three Preoxygenation Targets
title: "Comparison of Oxygen Reserve Index (ORI), End-Tidal Oxygen, and Time-Based Preoxygenation Targets With Arterial Blood Gas During Preoxygenation

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial was to learn whether the intensity of tongue-strengthening exercise affects tongue strength and swallowing in adults who have swallowing difficulty (dysphagia) 1 to 12 months after a stroke. The main questions it aimed to answer were:

* Does training at 80% or 100% of a person's maximum tongue pressure increase tongue strength more than usual care?
* Does training at 100% of maximum tongue pressure increase tongue strength more than training at 80%?
* Does either training intensity improve swallowing safety, throat residue after swallowing, the ability to eat by mouth, or swallowing-related quality of life?

Researchers compared the two exercise groups with a usual-care group that did not receive structured exercise.

Participants in the exercise groups pressed their tongue against an air-filled bulb (Iowa Oral Performance Instrument) three times a week for six weeks, with the target pressure updated every week. All participants had their tongue strength, tongue endurance and swallowing (by endoscopic swallowing examination) assessed before and after the six weeks. Participants in the exercise groups were assessed again four weeks later.
title: Submaximal Versus Maximal Isometric Tongue Training After Stroke

brief_summary:
Prolonged sitting during high-speed rail travel may contribute to subjective fatigue, musculoskeletal discomfort, sleepiness, reduced alertness, cognitive impairment, and changes in physiological and neurophysiological function.

This randomized crossover controlled trial aims to evaluate the effects of a standardized age-specific seated exercise program on multidimensional fatigue associated with prolonged sitting during simulated high-speed rail travel.

Participants aged 7 to 60 years will be analyzed within three prespecified age groups: 7-18 years, 18-45 years, and 45-60 years. Each participant will complete both a seated exercise condition and a prolonged sitting control condition in randomized order.

Outcome measures will include subjective fatigue, sleepiness, local discomfort, mood, attention, psychomotor vigilance, working memory, inhibitory control, heart rate variability, salivary biomarkers, surface electromyography, plantar pressure and postural control measures, and electroencephalographic indices.

The study aims to determine whether brief standardized seated exercise performed periodically during prolonged sitting can reduce fatigue and maintain physical, cognitive, autonomic, and neurophysiological function during simulated high-speed rail travel.
lead_sponsor: Aiyoudong Children and Youth Sports Health Research Institute
title: Effects of Seated Exercise on Fatigue Associated With Prolonged Sitting During High-Speed Rail Travel

The ACTION (Genotype-tAilored exerCise inTerventION) study investigated whether genetic information related to obesity susceptibility and endurance capacity could be used to inform personalized lifestyle interventions aimed at improving body mass index (BMI) and participation in physical activity programs.

Adults with increased genetic susceptibility to obesity and low habitual physical activity were invited to participate in an eight-week lifestyle intervention combining dietary counseling with physical activity recommendations.

The intervention initially compared structured jogging with recommendations to increase habitual physical activity. Following the evaluation of intervention completion, the exercise strategy was modified for a subsequent group of participants, incorporating a Genetic Endurance Score (GES) to guide allocation to jogging or yoga.

The study evaluated changes in BMI and completion of the assigned exercise programs, exploring the feasibility of integrating genetic information into personalized lifestyle recommendations.

brief_summary:
The goal of this prospective cohort study is to evaluate the long term clinical performance of the Kingstron X LINK bioprosthesis for aortic or mitral valve replacement, and verify whether its postoperative outcomes are non inferior to commercially available Medtronic Mosaic and Edwards Perimount Magna bioprostheses. It will also assess safety, hemodynamic performance and patient quality of life after valve implantation. The main questions it aims to answer are: Does the Kingstron X LINK bioprosthesis yield non inferior long term overall survival compared with Medtronic and Edwards bioprostheses? What are the differences in structural valve degeneration, adverse events, reoperation free survival and hemodynamic outcomes between the Kingstron X LINK and the comparator bioprostheses? How does patient quality of life differ across the three bioprosthesis groups during long term follow up? Researchers will compare patients receiving Kingstron X LINK bioprostheses against those receiving Medtronic Mosaic or Edwards Perimount Magna bioprostheses, all of whom underwent surgical aortic and/or mitral valve replacement at West China Hospital.

Participants will: Receive surgical aortic valve replacement and/or mitral valve replacement with one of the three types of bioprosthetic valves. Complete annual clinical follow up including clinical examination, hemodynamic assessment and quality of life evaluation. Be monitored for adverse events, structural valve degeneration and reoperation events over long term follow up.
primary_outcomes: Freedom from severe structural valve degeneration (SVD) at 5 years
title: Long-Term Performance of Kingstron X-LINK Compared With Commercial Bioprostheses

brief_summary:
Newborns routinely undergo heel stick procedures for blood screening tests shortly after birth. Although the procedure is brief, it can cause pain, stress, and physiological changes. Effective pain management is important because early painful experiences may affect newborn well-being and development.

Nonpharmacological methods are commonly used to reduce procedural pain in newborns because they are safe, easy to apply, and inexpensive. Two such methods are the ShotBlocker device, which provides tactile stimulation to reduce pain perception, and warm gel packs, which increase local blood flow and may improve comfort during the procedure. However, evidence regarding their effectiveness during heel stick procedures remains limited. This randomized controlled trial was conducted to compare the effects of ShotBlocker and warm gel pack applications during heel stick procedures in healthy term newborns. A total of 147 newborns were randomly assigned to a ShotBlocker group, a warm gel pack group, or a control group receiving routine care. The study evaluated procedural pain using the Neonatal Infant Pain Scale (NIPS), comfort using the Neonatal Comfort Behavior Scale, and physiological responses including heart rate, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, and heel temperature. The findings may help identify practical, noninvasive approaches to improve pain management and comfort during routine newborn procedures.
primary_outcomes: Neonatal Infant Pain Scale (NIPS) Score After Heel Stick Procedure
title: Effect of ShotBlocker and Warm Gel Pack on Heel Stick Pain in Newborns

brief_summary:
The goal of this multicenter retrospective observational study is to learn about the real-world safety and clinical effectiveness of disease-modifying therapy (DMT) in adults with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) due to Alzheimer's disease (AD) or AD dementia. The main questions it aims to answer are:

What are the safety outcomes of DMT, including amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA), adverse events, and infusion reactions (IRRs)? How do Clinical Dementia Rating (CDR) measures change in patients who receive DMT compared with those who do not?

Researchers will compare patients who receive DMT as part of their routine clinical care with patients who do not receive DMT to evaluate differences in clinical outcomes and safety.

Participants will not receive any study-assigned intervention or additional treatment as part of this study. Researchers will retrospectively collect existing clinical data, including cognitive and neuropsychiatric assessments, imaging findings, biomarker results, DMT use, and safety information.
title: Effectiveness and Safety of Disease-Modifying Therapy for Alzheimer's Disease: A Multicenter Retrospective Study

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to evaluate the therapeutic effects of combining active transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) with Action Observation Therapy (AOT) in pediatric patients diagnosed with spastic Cerebral Palsy. The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. Does combining tDCS with AOT yield significantly greater improvements in gross motor function (measured by GMFM-88) compared to AOT alone?
2. Does active tDCS paired with AOT lead to greater reductions in spasticity (MAS) and improvements in walking speed (10MWT) at 6 weeks post-intervention?

Researchers will compare participants receiving active tDCS plus AOT against a control group receiving sham tDCS plus AOT to isolate the synergistic effects of active brain stimulation.

Participants will:

1. Complete baseline clinical evaluations including gross motor, spasticity, and gait assessments.
2. Undergo scheduled intervention sessions consisting of tDCS administration combined with video-based Action Observation Therapy.
3. Attend follow-up assessment sessions at the end of the intervention period and 6 weeks post-intervention.
title: Additional Effects on tDCS With AOT on Lower Limb Functions on Children With Diplegic CP

brief_summary: This prospective observational study characterises the tumour immune microenvironment and microbial ecology of locally advanced rectal cancer before and during neoadjuvant therapy. Tumour tissue and peripheral blood are profiled by whole-genome sequencing, single-cell RNA sequencing with paired T-cell and B-cell receptor repertoire sequencing, spatial transcriptomics of formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded sections, multiplex immunofluorescence, and blood-based proteomic, cytokine and bulk T-cell receptor analyses. brief_summary: This study evaluates the mental workload and user experience associated with a Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) device called Exobots. The Exobots system uses a non-invasive electroencephalography (EEG) headset to detect neural signals and control a robotic glove that assists hand movement. The primary goal is to assess how three different system sensitivity levels (low, medium, high) impact mental effort, usability, and overall user perception. Healthy adult volunteers (students and staff from IFPR and UFPR) will participate in a single experimental session. During the session, they will perform a repeated mental imagery task (imagine hand movement) while the EEG records their brain activity. After each sensitivity block, participants will complete standardized questionnaires (NASA Task Load Index and User Experience Questionnaire) and a semi-structured qualitative interview about their experience. By combining objective neurophysiological data with subjective feedback, this research aims to identify optimal sensitivity thresholds that minimize cognitive strain and maximize user comfort. The findings are expected to provide technical recommendations for designing more adaptive, user-centered BCI systems for future neurorehabilitation applications.
primary_outcomes: EEG Theta/Beta Ratio as a Neurophysiological Marker of Cognitive Load
title: Neuroergonomic Analysis of a Brain-Computer Interface Device (BCI)

brief_summary: About 2 in every 100 Australian children have conduct disorder, a serious mental health condition characterised by antisocial behaviours like aggression and rule breaking. This condition leads to big problems not only for the children but also for their families. Despite its major impacts, conduct disorder is not well understood, and treatments are limited. Talk therapy works best, but it's hard to access and is expensive. Current medications can help but often cause unwanted side effects. Stimulant medications (like those used for Attention Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder or ADHD) may help reduce aggression and impulsive behavior in children with conduct disorder. One medication called lisdexamfetamine shows promise. It is safe and already approved for treating ADHD in children in Australia, and only needs to be taken once a day. Because it's safe and already in use for similar conditions, it could be a promising option for treating conduct disorder in children. This study will test if lisdexamfetamine can reduce conduct disorder symptoms in children aged 10 to 15 years old compared to placebo.
primary_outcomes: Nisonger Child Behavior Rating Form - Conduct Problem scale
title: Lisdexamfetamine For the Treatment of Conduct Disorder in Children

brief_summary:
A laryngeal mask airway is a medical device placed through the mouth to help patients breathe during general anaesthesia. It is commonly used during surgery. Usually, anaesthetists insert this device without directly seeing the opening of the airway. They check its position using breathing measurements, chest movements, and signs of air leakage. However, a device may appear to work normally even when it is not positioned correctly. Changes in head and neck position during surgery may also affect its placement.

The SaCo Video Laryngeal Mask Airway (SaCoVLM) is a newer airway device with a built-in camera that allows anaesthetists to see the opening of the airway and adjust the device's position.

The main aim of this study is to find out whether using the built-in camera to guide and adjust the SaCoVLM during insertion results in better airway positioning than the conventional method, which does not use the camera view. The researchers will also investigate whether the airway device remains correctly positioned when the patient's head and neck are moved.

This study will involve 70 adults aged 18 to 65 years who are scheduled for planned surgery under general anaesthesia at Universiti Malaya Medical Centre, Malaysia.

Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups, with an equal chance of being placed in either group:

* Group 1 (Video-guided insertion): The anaesthetist will use the SaCoVLM's built-in camera to guide insertion and adjust the device to achieve a better view of the airway opening.
* Group 2 (Conventional blind insertion): The anaesthetist will insert the same device using standard techniques and breathing tests without viewing the camera screen.

After successful insertion, researchers will assess the airway device in four head and neck positions: neutral, turned to the side, tilted backwards, and bent forwards.

The researchers will compare how often the airway opening is partly obscured in each group. They will also measure air leakage around the device, the time and number of attempts needed for insertion, changes in heart rate and blood pressure, and throat-related symptoms after surgery.

All procedures will be performed by experienced anaesthetists under standard monitoring during general anaesthesia. Participants will be assessed for throat-related complications approximately one hour after surgery.

The findings may help determine whether video-guided insertion provides better airway positioning than conventional insertion, particularly during head and neck movement. This information could help improve airway management and patient safety during future surgical procedures.
primary_outcomes: Incidence of Distorted Glottic View Following Head and Neck Repositioning
title: A Randomized Controlled SaCo-VLM Trial

brief_summary:
This study aims to investigate whether different doses of locally infiltrated lidocaine affect inflammation, neurological biomarkers, and cognitive function in patients undergoing major head and neck cancer surgery.

Major head and neck cancer surgery can cause substantial physical stress, inflammation, and changes in cognitive function after surgery. Lidocaine is a commonly used local anesthetic that may also have anti-inflammatory and protective effects on the nervous system. However, little is known about whether the dose of lidocaine injected into the surgical area influences these responses.

This prospective, randomized pilot study will include 20 adult patients undergoing head and neck cancer resection followed by microvascular free-flap reconstruction at University Medical Centre Ljubljana, Slovenia.

Participants will be randomly assigned to receive either 150 mg or 300 mg of lidocaine infiltrated into the surgical area at the beginning of surgery. Both groups will receive the same total volume of infiltration solution and the same dose of adrenaline.

Blood samples will be collected before surgery, six hours after surgical incision, and on postoperative days 1, 2, and 6 to measure inflammatory and neurological biomarkers. Cognitive function will be assessed before surgery, on postoperative day 6, and three months after surgery.

The study will explore whether the higher dose of lidocaine is associated with differences in inflammatory responses, neurological biomarkers, and postoperative cognitive function. The findings will help inform the design of larger future clinical studies.
primary_outcomes: Change in Serum Neuron-Specific Enolase (NSE) Concentration
Change in Serum S100 Beta (S100β) Protein Concentration
Change in Serum Glial Fibrillary Acidic Protein (GFAP) Concentration
Change in Serum Matrix Metalloproteinase-9 (MMP-9) Concentration
title: Lidocaine Infiltration and Neuroimmunomodulation in Head and Neck Cancer Surgery

brief_summary:
Superior semicircular canal dehiscence syndrome (SSCD), also known as Minor syndrome, is a rare otoneurological condition characterized by auditory and vestibular symptoms. Emerging evidence suggests a significant psychological burden, including anxiety, depressive symptoms, and suicidal ideation, potentially related to diagnostic delay and chronic symptomatology. However, no structured epidemiological study has systematically assessed quality of life and psychological symptoms in this population.

The aim of this study is to evaluate quality of life and associated psychological symptoms in adults reporting a diagnosis of SSCD using validated self-reported questionnaires in a national cross-sectional survey.
primary_outcomes: Overall quality of life score measured using the WHOQOL-BREF questionnaire
title: Functional Impact of Psychological Symptoms in Patients With Superior Semicircular Canal Dehiscence Syndrome (SSCD): a National Cross-sectional Study

brief_summary:
Background \& Objectives

Upper extremity paresis represents one of the most prevalent and debilitating neurological sequelae following stroke, severely compromising survivors' independence in activities of daily living (ADLs). Among evidence-based interventions, action observation therapy (AOT) and mirror therapy (MT) have demonstrated clinical efficacy in augmenting upper limb functional recovery. Concurrently, telerehabilitation has emerged as a promising modality due to its clinical efficacy, accessibility, and cost-effectiveness. However, no prior investigation has directly compared telerehabilitation-delivered AOT alone versus combined AOT with mirror therapy (AOT-MT) in subacute stroke. This study aims to evaluate and compare the therapeutic effects of these two digital intervention paradigms on upper limb motor recovery and functional outcomes.

Methods \& Technical Development

A proprietary cross-platform mobile web application ("Neuro-Mirror Pro") was developed and clinically deployed. The platform incorporates standardized 12-movement upper extremity training modules, client-side WebRTC and CSS image rendering ensuring strict privacy compliance without cloud video storage, and adherence-optimizing features including breakpoint-resume tracking logic.

Clinically, this study is a prospective, assessor-blinded, randomized controlled trial. Subacute stroke survivors with unilateral hemiparesis are recruited from an inpatient stroke rehabilitation ward. Eligible participants are stratified by baseline motor impairment severity (FMA-UE score) and the affected side (left vs. right hemiparesis), and subsequently randomized (1:1) to receive either app-based AOT alone or app-based combined AOT-MT. Both arms undergo a 4-week telerehabilitation intervention (36 minutes daily) in conjunction with conventional occupational therapy (1 hour daily on weekdays).

Outcome Measures

The primary outcome is upper extremity motor function assessed by the Fugl-Meyer Assessment for Upper Extremity (FMA-UE). Secondary outcomes include the modified Rankin Scale (mRS), Box and Block Test (BBT), ABILHAND questionnaire, short-form Quality of Movement Inventory (QMI), and app adherence/feasibility metrics. All outcomes are evaluated at baseline, 4 weeks (post-intervention), and 12 weeks (follow-up).
interventions: App-based combined action observation and mirror therapy
primary_outcomes: Change from Baseline in Fugl-Meyer Assessment for Upper Extremity (FMA-UE) Score
title: Web-Based Tele-Rehabilitation Using Action Observation and Mirror Therapy for Subacute Stroke: A Randomized Controlled Trial

brief_summary: This trial evaluates the safety and efficacy of SEEG recording and functional mapping for patients with drug-resistant epilepsy. It also assesses the safety and therapeutic effectiveness of SEEG-guided radiofrequency ablation for this patient group. The study will collect clinical evidence to support the standardized application of this combined diagnostic and treatment workflow for drug-resistant epilepsy.

brief_summary: Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) requires deep sedation, and propofol is commonly used because of its rapid onset and recovery, but it has a narrow therapeutic window, especially in elderly patients. Bispectral index (BIS) monitoring provides an objective, electroencephalography (EEG)-based measure of sedation depth. This prospective, randomized, single-blind study compares BIS-guided titration of propofol infusion (target BIS 40-60) with standard clinical titration in elderly patients (65 years and older, American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical status III) undergoing ERCP, with respect to total anesthetic consumption, recovery time, hemodynamic and respiratory complications, and endoscopist satisfaction.
title: Bispectral Index-Guided Propofol Sedation During Endoscopic Retrograde Cholangiopancreatography

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn if taking a probiotic supplement during pregnancy improves the body's response to insulin (insulin sensitivity) in pregnant women who were overweight or obese before pregnancy (body mass index ≥25 kg/m2). Reduced insulin sensitivity is common in these women and increases the risk of gestational diabetes mellitus and excessive fetal growth. Growing evidence suggests that the bacteria in the gut (gut microbiome) play a role in regulating blood sugar and insulin action.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Does a daily probiotic supplement improve insulin sensitivity in mid-pregnancy?
* Does it affect blood sugar levels, insulin production, the development of gestational diabetes mellitus, fetal growth and the gut bacteria of mothers and newborns?

Participants will:

* Take one sachet of the probiotic OMNi-BiOTiC® METAtox twice daily from early pregnancy until delivery (probiotic group only)
* Attend three study visits in early, mid and late pregnancy with blood tests, an oral glucose tolerance test (early and mid pregnancy), measurements of weight and blood pressure, and questionnaires on diet and physical activity
* Wear a glucose sensor on the upper arm for 10 days after each visit
* Provide stool samples at each visit and a first stool sample of their newborn
* Have fetal growth checked by ultrasound and pregnancy and birth outcomes recorded
primary_outcomes: Insulin sensitivity assessed by the PREDIM index
title: Effect of Probiotics on Insulin Sensitivity in Overweight and Obese Pregnancy

brief_summary: This study aims to evaluate the effects of cervicothoracic junction mobilization on pain, shoulder range of motion (ROM), and disability in patients with supraspinatus tendinitis. A randomized controlled trial will include 62 participants divided into experimental and control groups. The experimental group will receive cervicothoracic mobilization alongside conventional physiotherapy, while the control group will receive conventional physiotherapy only. Outcomes will be assessed using NPRS, a goniometer, and SPADI. Data will be analyzed using IBM SPSS, with results reported after data collection and analysis.
title: Effects of Cervicothoracic Mobilization in Patients With Supraspinatus Tendinitis

brief_summary:
This quasi-experimental study assessed the effectiveness of a structured, workplace-based core stability exercise program in reducing occupational low back pain (OLBP) among hospital nurses. Conducted at a tertiary care hospital in Islamabad, Pakistan, the study involved 146 registered nurses with OLBP, divided equally into an intervention group and a control group. The intervention group participated in a supervised core stability exercise regimen three times per week for four weeks, while the control group maintained routine occupational activities without structured exercise.

The core stability program emphasized neuromuscular control and strengthening of deep trunk stabilizing muscles, including the transversus abdominis, lumbar multifidus, pelvic floor muscles, diaphragm, and obliques. Each session incorporated warm-up, progressive core stability exercises, and cool-down phases, focusing on controlled movement quality over maximal effort. Exercises included abdominal drawing-in maneuvers, pelvic tilting, bridging, bird-dog, side bridge, and plank variations, with intensity progressively increased over the intervention period.

The study's rationale is grounded in Panjabi's spinal stability model, which identifies three interacting subsystems-passive (vertebrae, discs, ligaments), active (muscles, tendons), and neural control-that collectively maintain spinal stability. Occupational activities of nurses, such as manual patient handling, prolonged standing, and repetitive trunk movements, impose substantial biomechanical loads on the lumbar spine, often exceeding recommended safety limits and leading to cumulative tissue fatigue and injury. Core stability exercises target the active and neural control subsystems by enhancing deep trunk muscle activation and neuromuscular coordination, thereby improving spinal stiffness, load sharing, and movement efficiency, which collectively reduce mechanical stress on passive structures and alleviate pain.

The study's workplace-based intervention aligns with emerging evidence supporting exercise programs as effective non-pharmacological treatments for low back pain. While prior research has established core stability training benefits in chronic non-specific low back pain patients, this study addresses a gap by focusing on hospital nurses exposed to high occupational spinal loading. The pragmatic, supervised intervention demonstrated feasibility and safety, achieving full participant retention and no reported injuries.

Strengths include standardized intervention delivery, validated pain measurement, and comprehensive statistical analysis incorporating effect size estimation and sensitivity adjustment for confounders. Limitations consist of the non-randomized design, potential selection bias, imbalance in workplace department distribution, short intervention duration limiting long-term effect assessment, and reliance on self-reported pain without additional functional or biomechanical outcome measures.

Clinically, the findings advocate integrating structured core stability exercises into occupational health programs as a cost-effective strategy to mitigate OLBP, potentially reducing disability, absenteeism, and healthcare costs while enhancing nurse wellbeing and patient care quality. Future research should employ randomized controlled designs with extended follow-up and incorporate broader outcome measures such as functional capacity, muscle endurance, electromyographic activity, and quality of life to validate and extend these results.

title: Effectiveness of a Workplace-Based Core Stability Exercise Program in Reducing Occupational Low Back Pain Among Hospital Nurses: A Quasi-Experimental Study

brief_summary:
The study aims to address the gap between lifespan and healthspan (years of life free of age-related diseases and disabilities) by testing whether 2 approved U.S Food and Drug Administration (FDA) medications, dapagliflozin and semaglutide, can help people stay healthier as they age and delay the age-related functional decline. The study will test these medications over 36 months of treatment plus 6 months of observational follow up to see if they can safely maintain health and function during aging and eventually support their use for extending healthspan.

This study is being done because there are limited ways to slow down the age-related health and functional decline, and few reliable ways to measure early changes in healthspan in humans. The 2 study drugs have shown promising results in laboratory and early human studies, but more evidence is needed.
lead_sponsor: The University of Texas Health Science Center at San Antonio

brief_summary:
Cardiac rehabilitation is a comprehensive, multidisciplinary intervention aimed at reducing disability and improving functional recovery in patients following a cardiovascular event. In older patients, comprehensive multidimensional assessment using the Multidimensional Prognostic Index (MPI) provides a standardized approach to prognostic risk stratification.

The primary aim of this study is to determine whether an inpatient cardiac rehabilitation program implemented following a cardiovascular event can reduce the proportion of patients classified as being at high prognostic risk according to the MPI.

The study will also assess whether the benefits achieved through cardiac rehabilitation are maintained at the three-month follow-up. Finally, the study will evaluate the prognostic significance of changes in MPI score in response to the cardiac rehabilitation intervention.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of patients classified as being at high risk according to Multidimensional Prognostic Index (MPI)

brief_summary:
This study aims to evaluate whether a combination of a prebiotic (1-kestose) and a probiotic (Lacticaseibacillus rhamnosus BBH112) improves gastrointestinal symptoms and quality of life in adults with constipation-related symptoms.

A total of 40 adults aged 19 to 80 years will be enrolled in this randomized, double-blind, controlled trial. Participants will be randomly assigned to receive either the probiotic combined with the prebiotic or the probiotic combined with a placebo for 8 weeks.

The primary objective is to compare overall satisfaction with gastrointestinal symptom improvement between the two groups after 8 weeks. The study will also assess changes in abdominal pain, bloating, bowel habits, stool consistency, quality of life, and psychological well-being. In addition, changes in the gut microbiome will be evaluated using stool samples collected before and after the intervention.

The findings may help determine whether adding a prebiotic to probiotic supplementation provides additional benefits for adults experiencing constipation-related gastrointestinal symptoms.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Participants Satisfied With Overall Gastrointestinal Symptom Improvement
title: Effects of a Prebiotic-Probiotic Combination on Constipation Symptoms and Quality of Life

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to determine whether nasal continuous positive airway pressure (nCPAP) with neurally adjusted ventilatory assist (NAVA) backup ventilation (nCPAP-NAVA-backup mode) reduces the rate of severe apnea in extremely preterm infants ≤28 weeks' gestation compared with standard nasal continuous positive airway pressure (nCPAP mode). Severe apnea episodes is defined as breathing pause with oxygen levels ( SpO2) below 85% lasting at least 5 seconds and/or heart rate (HR) below 100 beats/minute lasting at least 5 seconds.

Each participant will receive both interventions in a randomized order, serving as their own control. The total duration of the intervention will be 24h. Each intervention period will last 12 hours. A washout period of 3 hours will be included between intervention periods to minimize potential carryover effects.

Randomized sequences to avoid order effects:

* Sequence A: nCPAP mode → nCPAP-NAVA-backup mode
* Sequence B: nCPAP-NAVA-backup mode →nCPAP mode
primary_outcomes: Number of severe apnea episodes per 9-hour observation period

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn if cell salvage lowers the need for donor blood in adults having planned heart surgery with a heart-lung machine. Cell salvage collects the blood a person loses during surgery, cleans it and gives it back to them. The hospital already has a programme to lower blood loss and the need for donor blood. Since January 2025, it uses cell salvage in all eligible people.

The main question it aims to answer is:

\- Do fewer participants need donor red blood cells during their hospital stay when cell salvage is used in everyone?

Researchers will compare people who had surgery with cell salvage from January 2025 to:

* people who had surgery in 2023 and 2024, before this change
* people who had surgery from January 2025 without cell salvage

to see if fewer of them need donor blood.

Researchers will also look at the use of other blood products, red blood cell levels, complications, time in hospital, and survival 12 months after surgery.

Participants will have their usual surgery and care. The study does not change their treatment. Researchers will collect information from their medical records, from surgery up to 12 months later.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of participants receiving allogeneic red blood cell transfusion
title: Systematic Intraoperative Cell Salvage in On-Pump Cardiac Surgery Within a Mature Patient Blood Management Programme

brief_summary: The study aims to compare Sensory Integration Therapy (SIT) with Conventional Physical Therapy (CPT) for improving gross motor function in children aged 4-10 years with mixed cerebral palsy. This randomized controlled trial plans to include 50 participants divided into two groups. Group A will receive Sensory Integration Therapy, while Group B will receive Conventional Physical Therapy over a 12-week intervention period. Outcomes will be assessed using the Gross Motor Function Measure (GMFM-88), Short Sensory Profile (SSP), and Parent-Reported Functional Independence \& Daily Activity Performance (PR-FADAP). Data will be analyzed using SPSS version 26, with statistical significance set at p \< 0.05. The study is expected to determine which intervention is more effective in improving gross motor function and sensory processing in children with mixed cerebral palsy.
primary_outcomes: Change in Gross Motor Function Measure-88 (GMFM-88) Score
title: Sensory Integration Therapy vs Conventional Physical Therapy in Children With Mixed Cerebral Palsy

brief_summary: The goal of this clinical trial is to test whether an individuation intervention can improve the quality of chronic kidney disease (CKD) care for patients with low socioeconomic status (SES) and to understand the mechanisms through which the intervention may improve care delivery and clinical outcomes. The study will involve nephrologists and their patients with CKD, with a focus on reducing healthcare disparities associated with low SES. Researchers will compare nephrologists who receive the individuation intervention with those in the control group to determine whether encouraging physicians to better understand their patients as unique individuals, rather than relying on assumptions associated with socioeconomic status, improves the quality of CKD care for patients with low SES.
primary_outcomes: Percentage of CKD quality metrics achieved
title: An Individuation Intervention to Reduce Socioeconomic Disparities in Chronic Kidney Disease Care

brief_summary:
Bruton's tyrosine kinase inhibitors (BTKis) have demonstrated substantial therapeutic efficacy across multiple B-cell malignancies. Their durable hematologic benefits confer a favorable benefit-risk profile compared with other treatments, positioning BTKis as a cornerstone of therapy in several B-cell malignancies. However, BTKis are associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular (CV) adverse events, ranging from common complications such as atrial fibrillation (AF) and hypertension to more severe outcomes, including ischemic MACE.

Accumulating evidence suggests that while CV toxicity is a class effect of BTKis, the incidence, magnitude, and risk of these events vary according to the specific agent used. Modest changes in systolic blood pressure or AF incidence and risk have been reported across BTKis in indirect comparisons; however, the clinical relevance of these findings remains uncertain, making it questionable to base BTKi selection solely on such differences. Moreover, if hematologic efficacy is assumed to be broadly comparable across BTKis and CV toxicity becomes the primary determinant of treatment choice, it would be logical to rely on robust, standardized CV endpoints traditionally used in the evaluation of CV therapies.

Taken together, these considerations highlight the need for direct comparisons between available BTKis to generate more robust cardiovascular evidence and ultimately guide hematologists toward selecting the least cardiotoxic agent. Although randomized controlled trials (RCTs) would be the ideal approach to address this question, no existing RCTs directly compare BTKis with cardiovascular events as a primary outcome. Recently, no significant differences in the risk of non-fatal MACE were observed among ibrutinib, acalabrutinib, and zanubrutinib, based on a network meta-analysis of safety outcomes from phase 3 RCTs primarily designed to assess BTKi efficacy . In this context, target trial emulation using observational data and propensity score-based methods offers a valuable alternative, enabling the generation of high-level evidence that closely approximates randomized conditions.

The primary objective of this study will therefore be to compare the risk of hospitalization for MACE among the three BTKis (ibrutinib, acalabrutinib, zanubrutinib) in patients with B-cell malignancies, using a nationwide target trial emulation framework based on the French National Health Data System (SNDS), which covers 98.8% of the French population.
title: MACE and BTK Inhibitors

Participants were randomly assigned to two groups. The intervention group performs resistance exercises in addition to a walking program, while the control group follows a walking program alone. Patients in the intervention group undergo resistance exercise sessions three days per week for 12 weeks. The primary outcomes are changes in ultrasonographic enthesitis scores measured using the Madrid Sonographic Enthesitis Index (MASEI) and Glasgow Ultrasound Enthesitis Scoring System (GUESS). Secondary outcomes include tendon stiffness assessed by shear-wave elastography, clinical enthesitis scores, disease activity, physical function, and quality of life. Outcomes are assessed at baseline and at week 12.

brief_summary:
Neonatal acute respiratory distress syndrome (NARDS) can be difficult to identify consistently because relevant information is distributed across clinical notes, imaging reports, and respiratory support records. This study will develop and validate an explainable system that organizes routinely collected electronic health record information and identifies infants whose clinical findings are compatible with NARDS.

The study will involve three neonatal intensive care units in China. Historical records from the lead center will be used for system development. A later period at the lead center and independent records from the two collaborating centers will be used for temporal and geographic validation. After the system has been locked, newly eligible infants will be included in a prospective validation phase without changing their clinical care.

System results will be compared with an independent reference assessment by neonatal intensive care specialists. The specialists will classify each infant's first eligible respiratory event as a high-likelihood NARDS-compatible clinical phenotype, a non-compatible clinical phenotype, clinically uncertain, or insufficient information. The study will evaluate sensitivity, specificity, predictive values, review workload, and the ability to identify insufficient information. During prospective validation, system results will remain unavailable to treating clinicians. The system is being evaluated as a research screening and review tool; it is not intended to replace a full clinical diagnosis or to determine treatment.
lead_sponsor: Guangzhou Women and Children's Medical Center
primary_outcomes: Sensitivity of high-priority review for the high-likelihood NARDS-compatible clinical phenotype
title: Development and Multicenter Validation of an Explainable System for Neonatal ARDS-Compatible Phenotyping

brief_summary:
This observational study aims to evaluate static and dynamic postural control in patients with carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS) according to electrophysiological disease severity and to compare their balance performance with that of healthy controls.

A total of 96 participants will be recruited into four groups: healthy controls and patients with mild, moderate, or severe CTS classified according to the Bland electrophysiological grading system.

Postural control will be assessed using the TecnoBody ProKin balance system under eyes-open and eyes-closed conditions. Additional assessments will include nerve conduction parameters, the Boston Carpal Tunnel Questionnaire, sensory function, handgrip strength, and pinch strength.

The primary objective is to determine whether the effect of visual condition on center-of-pressure sway area differs across the four study groups.
primary_outcomes: Change in Center-of-Pressure Sway Area Between Eyes-Open and Eyes-Closed Conditions
title: Postural Control and Balance Performance in Patients With Carpal Tunnel Syndrome

brief_summary:
Mechanical ventilation can lead to pulmonary, diaphragmatic, and hemodynamic complications due to an increase in global and regional transpulmonary pressure. Optimizing protective mechanical ventilation by using low tidal volumes and positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP), or by positioning the patient in prone position, is recommended to limit these effects.

Prone positioning during mechanical ventilation results in: i) a decrease in airway resistance; ii) a decrease in thoracic compliance, which leads to a redistribution of ventilation-perfusion ratios and, consequently, more homogeneous ventilation. In adults with acute respiratory distress syndrome, prone position reduces mortality and the duration of ventilation. The physiological benefits of prone position, along with its ease of implementation in children, make its use common in pediatrics. However, the clinical benefit of this practice in children has never been demonstrated. The effect of prone position is, hard to predict and varies from one patient to another. The heterogeneity of children in terms of age and respiratory mechanics highlights the importance of individualizing mechanical ventilation in this population, in order to identify which children might benefit from this practice.

Thoracic electrical impedance tomography (EIT) is the only technique that allows for real-time, noninvasive, and radiation-free assessment of pulmonary ventilation distribution at the patient's bedside. In children, it can be easily performed without any additional risk. In this population, a few studies have described the heterogeneity of lung volumes induced by recruitment maneuvers or different ventilation settings using thoracic electrical impedance.

The impact of the response to prone positioning on the improvement of global and regional respiratory mechanics has not yet been evaluated.

This study is a comparative cohort study (with each subject serving as their own control) conducted in the pediatric intensive care unit at Necker-Enfants Malades Hospital in Paris, France.
interventions: Thoracic electric impedance tomography to assed regional ventilation
primary_outcomes: Change in regional lung ventilation distribution
title: Regional Lung Ventilation During Prone Position in in Intubated Children

brief_summary:
This study evaluates the effectiveness and safety of transvaginal radiofrequency ablation of myomas (TVRFAM), a minimally invasive treatment for uterine fibroids performed at our clinic as part of the study.

Women with uterine fibroids who meet the study eligibility criteria are invited to participate. The study includes women with fibroids classified as FIGO types 3-5, measuring 2-10 cm in diameter. Up to three fibroids may be treated during a single procedure. Written informed consent is obtained from all participants before enrollment.

Before treatment, participants complete the Uterine Fibroid Symptom and Quality of Life (UFS-QOL) questionnaire, which assesses fibroid-related symptoms and their impact on daily life.

Participants are followed for 12 months after treatment, with follow-up visits at 1, 3, 6, and 12 months. At each visit, a transvaginal ultrasound examination is performed to measure the volume of the treated fibroids. Participants also complete the UFS-QOL questionnaire to assess changes in their symptoms and quality of life over time.

Complications occurring during the procedure are recorded. Information on pain after treatment, the duration of pain-relieving medication use, and any postoperative complications or other unwanted effects is also collected during follow-up.

The main aim of the study is to measure the percentage reduction in fibroid volume following treatment. The study also evaluates changes in symptoms and quality of life, pain after the procedure, use of pain-relieving medication, and any complications or unwanted effects during the 12-month follow-up period.
primary_outcomes: Percentage change in fibroid volume at 6 months after the intervention
title: Prospective Study of TVRFA Treatment for FIGO Type 3-5 Uterine Fibroids

brief_summary:
Effectiveness of Oxitard Gel Versus Physiotherapeutic and Pharmacological Interventions in Alleviating Oral Submucous Fibrosis: A Phase-II Randomized Control Trial

Background Oral Submucous Fibrosis (OSMF) is a chronic, potentially malignant disorder of the oral mucosa. It causes progressively restricted mouth opening, reduced tongue protrusion with depapillation, submucosal fibrosis, blanching and loss of mucosal elasticity, and a shrunken uvula. It most often affects the buccal mucosa, palate and retromolar region, followed by the faucial pillars and pharynx. It is most common in South Asia. Areca nut chewing is the main cause, and commercial products such as gutka, pan masala and mawa add to the burden. Iron, vitamin B12 and folate deficiencies and capsaicin from chillies may also contribute.

Irritants in areca nut and chillies trigger a juxta-epithelial inflammatory reaction. This shows first as burning, then vesicles, then ulceration. The epithelium becomes atrophic and poorly vascularised, so it heals poorly and scars. That scarring produces the fibrosis that restricts mouth opening, tongue movement and cheek flexibility. Treatment begins with stopping the habit. Early and intermediate cases are managed without surgery, usually with oral physiotherapy as an add-on.

Operational Definition (Haider et al.)

Clinical staging: Stage 1 is faucial bands only, Stage 2 is faucial and buccal bands, and Stage 3 is faucial, buccal and labial bands.

Functional staging: Stage A is mouth opening of 20 mm or more, Stage B is 11-19 mm, and Stage C is 10 mm or less.

Aim and Objectives

The study compares conventional treatment (physiotherapy exercises plus multivitamins) with contemporary treatment (a novel herbal gel and Shekar's intraoral appliance) in OSMF patients. Its objectives are:

Record sociodemographic and clinical features to categorise patients. Assess how well the herbal gel works. Assess how well Shekar's appliance works. Compare both contemporary treatments with conventional therapy.

Hypotheses

Null: there is no difference between conventional and contemporary treatments. Alternate: there is a significant difference between them.

Methodology

Design: pilot randomised controlled trial. Setting: Department of Oral Medicine, Dow International Dental College (DIDC), Karachi. Patients come from DIDC Hospital and Dr. Ishrat-ul-Ibad Khan Institute of Oral Health Sciences.

Inclusion: OSMF patients with limited mouth opening, burning, fibrotic bands and blanched mucosa, in Haider Clinical Stages 1-2 and Functional Stages A-B.

Exclusion: leukoplakic, erythroplakic or speckled lesions, non-healing ulcers or suspected malignancy; TMJ dysfunction; psychiatric disorders; other lesions that cause burning; and hypersensitivity to any ingredient of the gel or vitamins.

Sample and allocation: 5 patients per group, 20 in total. The size was calculated in OpenEpi (95% confidence, 80% power). Patients are recruited by consecutive sampling and assigned to groups by a computer-generated random sequence.

Herbal gel: made by Nutrimed Laboratories. It contains 1% each of Nigella sativa, tulsi, aloe vera, curcumin and lycopene, plus 0.1% vitamin E, in a carbomer 974P base.

Data Collection and Blinding

The study needs IRB approval from DUHS, and every participant gives written informed consent. Oral Medicine staff who are not on the research team do the examinations. A dental assistant keeps the group allocation sealed until the results are complete. Participants are not told which treatment they receive. The outcomes are:

Mouth opening: measured between the incisors with a vernier caliper Burning sensation: Visual Analogue Scale (VAS) Cheek flexibility: measured at rest and with cheeks blown; the difference is recorded Tongue protrusion: in mm Mucosal colour: digital photographs Complete Blood Count: at the start and end of the study

Intervention Groups

Group 1: physiotherapy 3 times a day for 30 minutes, plus Pentovit H twice daily.

Group 2: physiotherapy plus the herbal gel 3 times a day, with nothing to eat or drink for 30 minutes after each application.

Group 3: Shekar's appliance 3 times a day for 15 minutes, plus Pentovit H. Group 4: Shekar's appliance 3 times a day for 15 minutes, plus the herbal gel 3 times a day.

Patients log their compliance on record sheets that don't name their treatment.

Follow-up, Duration and Analysis Patients are reviewed every 15 days for 3 months (6 visits), with a final CBC at the end. The study will take 9-12 months. Paired t-tests will measure change within each group, and unpaired t-tests will compare the groups, with p \< 0.05 counted as significant.

brief_summary:
Uterine atony and postpartum hemorrhage are important causes of maternal morbidity and mortality following cesarean section. Oxytocin is routinely administered to stimulate uterine contractions and prevent postpartum uterine atony. However, higher doses, particularly when administered rapidly, may produce cardiovascular effects such as vasodilatation, hypotension, reflex tachycardia, and increased cardiac output. Previous studies comparing low-dose and high-dose oxytocin have reported conflicting findings regarding adequate uterine contractions and blood loss. Therefore, further investigation is required to determine the comparative effectiveness of different oxytocin doses during elective cesarean section.

The objective of this randomized controlled trial is to compare the effects of two different doses of intravenous oxytocin (5 IU and 10 IU) in patients undergoing elective cesarean section in terms of adequate uterine contractions and blood loss.

The study will be conducted in the Department of Obstetrics and Gynecology, Shalamar Hospital, Lahore, over six months after approval of the synopsis. A total of 120 pregnant women will be enrolled through non-probability consecutive sampling. Eligible participants will be aged 18-35 years, with a gestational age of 37-42 weeks, ASA physical status I or II, uncomplicated pregnancies, and scheduled for elective cesarean section under spinal anesthesia. Women with active labour, multiple pregnancy, premature rupture of membranes, pregnancy-induced hypertension, preeclampsia, increased bleeding risk, coagulation abnormalities, thrombocytopenia, or oxytocin hypersensitivity will be excluded.

After obtaining informed written consent, participants will be randomly allocated through the lottery method into two equal groups. Group A (n=60) will receive 5 IU intravenous oxytocin, while Group B (n=60) will receive 10 IU intravenous oxytocin at the time of umbilical cord clamping. The assigned dose will be diluted in 1,000 ml of normal saline or Ringer's lactate solution and administered according to the approved study protocol. All procedures will be performed by the same team to minimize procedural variation.

The primary outcomes will be adequate uterine contractions and blood loss. Adequate uterine contractions will be defined as at least one contraction at three minutes, lasting 40-60 seconds, with sufficient intensity to make the uterus feel firm on palpation. Blood loss will be measured by combining blood collected in a kidney tray and measured using a graduated cylinder with blood retained on gauze, estimated through weight difference. Secondary observations will include nausea, vomiting, hypotension, and headache.

Data will be analyzed using SPSS version 26. Numerical variables will be presented as mean and standard deviation, while categorical variables will be presented as frequencies and percentages. The chi-square test will be used for group comparisons of categorical outcomes. Stratification will be performed according to age, gestational age, and body mass index. A p-value of ≤0.05 will be considered statistically significant.

The study will help determine the comparative effectiveness of 5 IU and 10 IU intravenous oxytocin in achieving adequate uterine contractions and controlling blood loss during elective cesarean section.
title: Comparison of Effect of Two Different Doses of Intravenous Oxytocin on Patients Undergoing Elective Cesarean Section

brief_summary: This is a multicenter, prospective, observational pilot cohort study in patients with surgically resected non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC, pathologic stage IA3-IIIA). Whole exome sequencing (WES) of each patient's resected tumor tissue and matched normal blood (buffy coat) is used to build a patient-specific (tumor-informed) minimal residual disease (MRD) panel, after excluding germline and clonal hematopoiesis variants. MRD is then assessed in paired plasma circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) and bronchial washing fluid (BWF) ctDNA collected at 6, 12, 18 and 24 months after surgery. The study evaluates whether MRD positivity in plasma and/or BWF is associated with subsequent clinical or radiologic recurrence, compares MRD detection rates and quantitative values between plasma and BWF, and explores the lead time of MRD detection relative to standard surveillance with chest CT and serum CEA. MRD results are not used to confirm recurrence or to change treatment; all clinical decisions follow standard of care. Forty participants will be enrolled at three Severance hospitals in Korea.

brief_summary:
The Study of Psychoeducation and Reading for Kids (SPARK) is a trial of a broad-spectrum psychoeducational tutoring intervention. The goal of the study is to assess how much the intervention affects reading skills and psychological functioning. Children ages 6 through 10 who are in need of improvement in reading skills and/or psychological skills will be recruited. The intervention consists of 30 minute telephone sessions delivered 5 or 6 times a week, for at least a year, by trained tutors, who are not therapists, counselors, or other licensed health care providers. The intervention makes use of manuals to be read aloud (in "alternate reading") by tutors and students, psychological skills exercises carried out by tutor and student together, and social conversation between tutor and student. The curriculum covers psychological health skills, such as productivity, joyousness, kindness, fortitude, decision-making, conflict-resolution, friendship-building, self-discipline, courage, and others. The psychological skills approach is a "strength-based" approach to mental health. This approach emphasizes the positive patterns that are the opposites of the maladaptive patterns that lead to psychiatric diagnoses.

Children's reading about these skills furnishes practice in reading, which in itself is seen as a psychological competence that increases a child's positive experience of school, and therefore of life. For children not ready to practice by reading text, the intervention also includes a curriculum for teaching reading, including, if necessary, phonemic and spatial awareness, which are important foundation skills. Once the students are capable of reading connected text, all the readings in the curriculum are meant to teach them psychological skills as well as to provide reading practice.

Every six months, measures will be taken of the child's behavioral and emotional well-being and of reading skill.

This is a single-arm study, meaning that all research participants will receive the same intervention -- there is no random assignment and no inactive treatment group.

primary_outcomes: Slosson Oral Reading Test, Third Edition

brief_summary: Appendectomy is one of the most frequently performed surgical procedures worldwide and remains the gold standard treatment for acute appendicitis. Although laparoscopic surgery offers advantages such as less pain, faster recovery, and shorter hospital stays compared to open techniques, postoperative pain caused by visceral stimulation from pneumoperitoneum and tissue trauma is still inevitable. Inadequate analgesia delays the recovery process, whereas high-dose opioid use leads to complications such as nausea, vomiting, and respiratory depression. Therefore, within the framework of Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) protocols, multimodal analgesia methods and interfacial plane blocks that reduce opioid consumption have gained prominence. The Transversus Abdominis Plane (TAP) block is an effective regional anesthesia technique where a local anesthetic is injected into the fascial plane between the internal oblique and transversus abdominis muscles. Initially described using anatomical landmarks, this method has become widely used with the addition of ultrasound guidance. The TAP block features different modalities, including subcostal, lateral, posterior, dual, and surgeon-performed laparoscopic-assisted approaches. While the subcostal approach targets the supraumbilical (T7-9) region, the lateral and posterior approaches block the infraumbilical (T10-L1) nerve branches. In recent years, the transperitoneal approach, performed by the surgeon under direct vision during laparoscopic surgery, has gained popularity. This technique is performed by advancing the needle through the parietal peritoneum into the transversus abdominis muscle. Due to direct visualization, the risk of visceral injury decreases, and the success rate of delivering the drug to the correct fascial plane increases. This study aims to evaluate and compare the efficacy of surgeon-performed laparoscopic-assisted transversus abdominis plane block versus standard intravenous analgesia in patients undergoing laparoscopic appendectomy.
