brief_summary:
Background:

Perimesencephalic subarachnoid hemorrhage (pmSAH) is a distinct subtype of traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH) characterized by a localized bleeding pattern around the midbrain not resulting from a ruptured aneurysm of a posterior circulation main artery. Traditionally considered benign with generally good prognosis, pmSAH has been attributed to a presumed venous etiology. However, recent advances in imaging technology have led to the identification of previously occult vascular lesions, most notably basilar artery perforator aneurysms (BAPAs) that may present a potential cause in a subset of patients with pmSAH. Preliminary data from the international PERFAN registry which retrospectively included 148 patients with ruptured BAPAs, challenge the benign perception of pmSAH as a whole. Interestingly, in this biggest case collection so far, patients diagnosed with BAPAs experienced significantly higher rates of complications and worse functional outcomes compared to cases of non-aneurysmal pmSAH (NA-pmSAH). To date, prospective data on prevalence, presentation and outcome of BAPA-associated pmSAH (BAPA-pmSAH) is missing, thus complicating decisions on management of this increasingly diagnosed entity.

Aims:

The DECIPHER-pmSAH study aims to establish a prospective registry to:

1. determine and compare the prevalence of BAPA-pmSAH and non-aneurysmal pmSAH
2. compare short-term and mid-term functional outcomes between patients with BAPA-pmSAH and those with non-aneurysmal pmSAH
3. evaluate the rate and nature of complications in both these pmSAH subgroups
4. enhance the understanding of radiological features associated with pmSAH, with the aim of distinguishing between BAPA-pmSAH and non-aneurysmal pmSAH
5. characterize observed treatment strategies and their outcomes, comparing conservative and active management approaches

Design:

The DECIPHER-pmSAH is a prospective, multicenter, observational study. For an adequately powered study, we are aiming at enrollment of at least 264 patients over the course of three years, starting on January 1st, 2026. For recruiting participating sites, we are aiming to build upon the previously established collaboration with multiple international centers contributing to the PERFAN registry, in which cases of perforator aneurysms were retrospectively collected.

Methods:

This study will include cases of atraumatic pmSAH where no aneurysm of main arteries of the posterior circulation was detected. Predefined diagnostic workup criteria must be met for patient enrollment, including cross-sectional imaging (CT or MRI) at baseline, whenever possible and clinically justified at least one digital subtraction angiography (DSA) with high-resolution three-dimensional rotational angiography (3D-RA) and collection of clinical data at index presentation, hospital discharge and 90 days follow-up. Anonymized imaging data will be centrally analyzed by trained neuroradiologists, blinded to clinical data in a core lab at the Inselspital, Bern. The primary endpoint to be examined is the prevalence of ruptured BAPA and non-aneurysmal hemorrhage in cases of pmSAH. Secondary and tertiary endpoints include clinical outcomes at 90 days after index presentations and specific radiological findings respectively.
interventions: Completion of a patient-reported outcome measure (PROM) in the form of a EQ-5D questionnaire
lead_sponsor: Insel Gruppe AG, University Hospital Bern
primary_outcomes: Rate of BAPAs in pmSAH where at least one high-resolution 3D-rotational angiography (3D-RA) of the dominant vertebral artery was performed within 7 days after the index presentation
title: Determining the Clinical Impact and Prevalence of Hemorrhagic Subtypes in Perimesencephalic Subarachnoid Hemorrhage

brief_summary:
This study examines whether the size of the jugular foramen is associated with atrial fibrillation, a common irregular heart rhythm. The jugular foramen is an opening at the base of the skull through which nerves involved in heart regulation and a major vein pass.

This retrospective study uses existing medical records and head computed tomography (CT) scans from 240 adults aged 60-90 years: 120 with atrial fibrillation and 120 without a history of atrial fibrillation. Researchers measure the jugular foramina on both sides of the skull and compare their estimated volumes between the groups. They also examine whether any association remains after accounting for age, sex, skull size, other medical conditions, and heart ultrasound findings.

No additional scans, treatments, or patient visits are performed for this study. The study assesses an association and cannot establish whether jugular foramen size causes atrial fibrillation.
lead_sponsor: Ankara Ataturk Sanatorium Training and Research Hospital
title: From Skull Base to Atrial Fibrillation: Reduced Jugular Foramen Volume as a Structural Correlate of Atrial Fibrillation

brief_summary: The purpose of this study is to learn what happens to MK-6916 in a person's body when given to participants with moderate or severe kidney impairment compared to healthy participants.
primary_outcomes: Area Under the Concentration-Time Curve from Time 0 to 12 Hours (AUC0-12) of MK-6916 on Day 16
title: A Clinical Trial of MK-6916 in Participants With Moderate and Severe Kidney Disease Compared to Healthy Controls (MK-6916-013)

brief_summary:
This study will evaluate whether a single oral dose of tizanidine 4 mg given before surgery improves laryngeal mask airway (LMA) insertion conditions and postoperative recovery in adults undergoing elective ambulatory surgery under sevoflurane-based general anesthesia.

Eligible adults aged 18 to 65 years with American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) physical status I or II will be randomly assigned to receive either oral tizanidine 4 mg or a matching placebo 60 to 90 minutes before anesthesia induction. Participants and the clinical and outcome-assessment teams will be blinded to treatment allocation.

The primary outcome is the proportion of participants with excellent LMA insertion conditions at the first insertion attempt, assessed using a predefined composite score. Secondary outcomes include anesthetic and opioid requirements, hemodynamic changes, emergence and recovery times, postoperative pain, quality of recovery, and adverse effects.

The study aims to determine whether tizanidine premedication improves airway insertion conditions and recovery outcomes without unacceptable adverse effects.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Patients with Excellent Laryngeal Mask Airway (LMA) Insertion Conditions at First Attempt
title: Tizanidine Premedication Versus Placebo for Laryngeal Mask Airway Insertion and Recovery in Adults Undergoing Ambulatory Surgery

brief_summary:
The goal of this randomized clinical trial is to learn how alcohol use, cannabis use, and using both substances affect whether and how quickly people stop a video being shown to a woman. The study will recruit 312 people from the Metro-Denver area who drink alcohol and use cannabis; half of the participants will be women. The main questions it aims to answer are:

* How do alcohol, cannabis, and their combined use affect whether participants stop the video and how quickly they do so?
* Does alcohol use versus alcohol and cannabis use by others in the scenario affect whether and how quickly participants stop the video?

Researchers will compare four randomly assigned groups: alcohol only, cannabis only, both alcohol and cannabis, and neither substance. Participants will also be randomly assigned to one of two scenarios involving alcohol use or alcohol and cannabis use by others. These comparisons will help researchers understand how participants' own substance use and substance use by others affect their decisions to intervene.

Participants will:

* Complete a phone call to review the study and schedule a mobile laboratory visit at their home.
* Have their ID checked, complete a breath alcohol test to confirm no alcohol is in their system, and be weighed. Female participants will also take a pregnancy test.
* Provide written consent and complete questionnaires so researchers can confirm eligibility before random assignment.
* Follow their assigned substance-use condition. Participants in the cannabis-only group will smoke their usual cannabis at home while staff monitor them through Zoom. Those in the alcohol-only group will drink two weight-based alcoholic beverages, with a target blood alcohol concentration of 0.08%. Those assigned to both substances will use cannabis first and then drink alcohol. Those assigned to neither substance will not use either as part of the study.
* Provide blood and breath samples to measure cannabis-related THC and alcohol levels.
* Complete a task in which they can choose to stop a video being shown to a woman. Researchers will measure whether they stop the video and how long they take to do so.
* Take part in a recorded interview about their experience and the reasons they did or did not stop the video. Researchers will analyze these interviews to better understand how substance use affects decisions.
* Answer questions about what they believed the study was testing and their impressions of the other participants, receive an explanation of the study, and receive compensation.
title: Substance Use and Media Preferences

brief_summary:
This study examines how accurately a smartphone can measure the rhythmic rise and fall of heart rate that occurs with breathing (respiratory heart rate variability).

Healthy adult volunteers attend one laboratory visit of about 90 minutes in Seoul, Republic of Korea. While seated, each participant breathes freely for 5 minutes, then follows audio-guided breathing at seven slow rates between 4 and 7 breaths per minute in random order and finally at 15 breaths per minute, with 2-minute rests between conditions (31 minutes of recording and 16 minutes of rest). During every condition, a single iPhone measures the face with its front camera (contact-free measurement) and a fingertip lightly placed over its rear camera lens (contact measurement) at the same time; no video is stored. A chest ECG and a respiratory belt record continuously throughout the session as references.

The main question is how closely the breathing-related heart rate variability amplitude measured from the face agrees with the ECG during slow paced breathing. The study also compares the fingertip measurement with the ECG, reports how often the smartphone measurements fail to produce a usable value, evaluates standard heart rate variability measures, and explores whether shorter recordings would give similar agreement and how breathing rate affects agreement.

The smartphone app is a research prototype used only for data collection. This study does not test a treatment, and its measurements are not used to diagnose or treat participants.
interventions: Smartphone simultaneous facial and fingertip photoplethysmography (research app)
primary_outcomes: Log Ratio of Facial Remote Photoplethysmography to ECG Respiratory Heart Rate Variability Amplitude During Slow Paced Breathing
title: Smartphone Camera Measurement of Breathing-Related Heart Rate Variability Compared With ECG in Healthy Adults

brief_summary:
The study was designed as a randomized controlled, single-blind study. Power analysis was used to calculate the sample size. A 3-group one-way ANOVA test was used for the power analysis. The power analysis result determined a total of n=51 participants, with n=17 in each group.

The study included 51 BPPV patients who presented to the Ear, Nose, and Throat Outpatient Clinics of Afyon Health Sciences University, Health Application and Research Center, were diagnosed with posterior canal BPPV by a specialist physician, met the inclusion criteria, and volunteered to participate. Participants were divided into 3 groups. To prevent potential bias in the study results, the distribution of participants into groups was performed using stratified randomization. Patients were distributed into all 3 groups in a way that ensured similar age, gender, and number of previous attacks. At the beginning of the study, all participants underwent sociodemographic evaluation, the Dizziness Disability Inventory, the Vertigo Symptom Scale, and balance assessment using Kinvent Plates. After the assessments, all participants underwent the Epley maneuver. The first study group received VR in addition to the Epley maneuver. The second study group received exergaming in addition to the Epley maneuver. Both study groups received VR or exergaming for 30 minutes, twice a week, for 6 weeks. At the end of 6 weeks, the same assessments were repeated, and patients were compared before and after treatment. The control group received the Epley maneuver after the initial assessments. They were called back for a follow-up after 6 weeks, and the same assessments were performed on them as well.
title: Exergaming for Residual Dizziness and Balance in BPPV

brief_summary: This randomized controlled trial will compare structured telerehabilitation with clinic-based physiotherapy in children aged 4-12 years with spastic cerebral palsy. Both groups will receive physiotherapy three times per week for 12 weeks. The study will evaluate changes in gross motor function using the Gross Motor Function Measure (GMFM-88), assess spasticity using the Modified Ashworth Scale (MAS), and examine the usability of telerehabilitation using the Telehealth Usability Questionnaire (TUQ). The study aims to determine whether structured telerehabilitation can provide an effective alternative to clinic-based physiotherapy while potentially reducing barriers related to travel, cost, and access to pediatric rehabilitation services.
primary_outcomes: Change in Gross Motor Function Measure-88 (GMFM-88) Score
title: Telerehabilitation Compared With Clinic-Based Physiotherapy in Children With Spastic Cerebral Palsy

brief_summary:
Background:

Dopamine is a chemical that the brain makes when a person expects a reward. Researchers want to learn more about how eating different types of food affects dopamine levels in the brain.

Objective:

To test how eating different foods affects dopamine levels in the brains of healthy people.

Eligibility:

Healthy people aged 18 to 45 years old.

Design:

Participants will be divided into 2 groups (cohorts). Both will have overnight stays in the clinic.

All participants will be screened. They will talk to a dietitian about their eating habits. They will have a test of how much energy their body uses: They will lie on a table with a clear hood over their heads to measure the gases as they breathe.

During the 3 weeks before participants stay at the clinic, a dietitian will call at 3 random times to ask what they ate the day before. They will complete questionnaires. Cohort 1 will wear a device to track their step count for at least 7 days; these participants will be given food to eat for 2 days before they stay in the clinic.

Cohort 1 will stay in the clinic for 14 days. They will eat as much or as little as they would like on 2 different diets for 5 days each and a normal diet on the other days. They will have blood collected multiple times. They will have 2 d ifferent types of imaging scans. For 1 type, they will receive a drug through a vein to show how much dopamine is in their brains.

Cohort 2 will stay in the clinic for 2 days. They will eat only the foods provided. They will have imaging scans before and after drinking a milkshake. For both scans, they will receive a drug through a vein to show how much dopamine is in their brains. They will have blood collected multiple times.
lead_sponsor: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases (NIDDK)
primary_outcomes: Dopamine D2 receptor binding potential (D2BP) during steady portion of [11C]raclopride infusion PET neuroimaging
title: Effects of Ad Libitum Ultra-Processed Diet on Brain Dopamine in Humans

brief_summary: Subacromial impingement syndrome is a common cause of shoulder pain and difficulty with arm movements. This study compared two injection treatments: ultrasound-guided dextrose prolotherapy and corticosteroid injection. A total of 32 patients aged 20-55 years were randomly assigned to one of the two treatment groups. Both groups also received a home exercise program. Pain, shoulder-related pain and disability, and shoulder range of motion were assessed before treatment and at 1 and 3 months after treatment. Thirty patients completed the follow-up and were included in the final analysis. The aim was to compare the clinical outcomes of the two treatments over the 3-month follow-up period. The findings may help improve understanding of these treatment options for patients with subacromial impingement syndrome.
title: Subacromial Impingement Syndrome Ultrasound-Guided Dextrose Prolotherapy and Corticosteroid Injection

brief_summary: This study will test whether tailored nutritional support before surgery, alone or combined with a structured exercise program, can help adult patients recover better after surgery for colorectal (bowel) cancer. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of three groups: usual care, tailored nutritional support alone, or nutritional support combined with a structured exercise program (multimodal prehabilitation). The main goal is to find out whether either approach improves physical function 30 days after surgery, measured by how far participants can walk in 6 minutes (the 6-minute walk test). The study will also look at nutritional intake, physical function, quality of life, complications, hospital readmissions, and length of hospital stay. A total of 140 adult patients scheduled for surgery for colorectal cancer at hospitals in Northern Norway will be enrolled.
title: Tailored Nutrition vs. Exercise Prehabilitation Before Colorectal Cancer Surgery

brief_summary: The study aims to clinically assess the surface finish and periodontal response of injectable resin composite vs conventional resin composite in class V restorations and reevaluate after six months follow u. It is aim to answer which composite has no change in periodontal response, superior marginal integrity surface texture. Researcher will compare the two composites, and the participants will have the restorations in class V and get a follow up after 6 months.
title: Clinical and 3D Evaluation of Injectable Versus Conventional Composite in Class V Restorations

brief_summary: This prospective, single-arm study will evaluate whether thymosin alpha 1 treatment affects serum immunoglobulin M (IgM) levels in adults with sepsis. Participants will receive standard care plus thymosin alpha 1 1.6 mg by subcutaneous injection every 12 hours for 5 days. Blood samples will be collected before treatment and on days 1, 3, 5, and 7 to measure IgM and plasma microvesicles. The study aims to clarify whether thymosin alpha 1 may support early immune responses in sepsis.
title: Thymosin Alpha 1 and IgM Levels in Sepsis

brief_summary: This study aims to investigate the immediate effects of three intervention approaches in young adults with nonspecific low back pain. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of three groups: core stabilization exercises, whole-body vibration combined with core stabilization exercises, or cervical stabilization combined with core stabilization exercises. Outcomes will be assessed before and immediately after the intervention. The study will evaluate trunk motor control, pain intensity, pressure pain threshold, trunk muscle endurance, and balance. The purpose is to compare the immediate effects of these approaches and determine whether adding whole-body vibration or cervical stabilization to core stabilization produces additional benefits.
primary_outcomes: Trunk motor control (supine), Pressure Biofeedback Unit
Trunk motor control (prone; transversus abdominis activation), Pressure Biofeedback Unit
title: Effects of Whole-Body Vibration and Cervical Stabilization With Core Stabilization in Young Adults With Non-Specific Low Back Pain

brief_summary: This prospective observational study aims to evaluate whether an intensive tele-tobacco cessation program delivered through the PROMETHEE platform improves smoking cessation among smokers participating in the French national lung cancer screening pilot program IMPULSION. Participants receiving the PROMETHEE pathway will be compared with matched controls receiving standard smoking cessation support available through IMPULSION. The primary endpoint is self-reported smoking cessation at 12 months.
title: PROMETHEE: A Shared Interregional Tele-Tobacco Cessation Platform Embedded Within the IMPULSION Lung Cancer Screening Program

brief_summary: This is a prospective, single-arm observational diagnostic study without therapeutic intervention or control arm. Participants undergo diagnostic assessment for SIBO including lactulose hydrogen/methane breath testing and gastroduodenoscopy with collection of small intestinal luminal aspirate, mucus and mucosal biopsies, as well as stool, saliva and venous blood sampling. Gastroduodenoscopy is performed only when clinically indicated and is not performed solely for study purposes. During the clinically indicated endoscopic procedure, two additional mucosal biopsies are obtained for study-specific analyses.
interventions: Gastroduodenoscopy, luminal aspirate, mucosal biopsies, collection of mucus, lactulose breath test
lead_sponsor: Insel Gruppe AG, University Hospital Bern
primary_outcomes: prevalence of SIBO in premenopausal women with endometriosis
title: Prevalence of Small Intestinal Bacterial Overgrowth (SIBO) in Women With Endometriosis

brief_summary: The primary purpose of this study is to evaluate the safety and tolerability of treprostinil administered with a soft mist inhaler (SMI) over 16 weeks in approximately 40 participants with PH-COPD.
conditions: Pulmonary Hypertension Associated With Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease
primary_outcomes: Incidence of serious adverse events, severe adverse events, cardiopulmonary hospitalizations, and deaths
title: Study of Treprostinil Administered Via Soft Mist Inhaler (SMI) in Participants With Pulmonary Hypertension Associated With Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (PH-COPD)

brief_summary: Hidradenitis suppurativa (HS) is a chronic inflammatory disease affecting approximately 1% of the population. Most pathophysiological studies have focused on advanced forms (Hurley II-III), which obscures the initial mechanisms. The mean diagnostic delay of 7 to 10 years and the lack of prognostic biomarkers limit early management. Identifying molecular and microbiological alterations as early as Hurley stage I could allow stratification of the risk of progression and support early intervention strategies.
primary_outcomes: Identification of a combined molecular and microbiological signature associated with Hurley stage I hidradenitis suppurativa
title: Early Pathophysiology of Hidradenitis Suppurativa and Prediction of the Risk of Progression: a Prospective Cohort

brief_summary:
The goal of this prospective, randomized, open-label, controlled clinical trial is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of rutin combined with vitamin C (Ruta C) and vitamin C alone as adjunctive therapies in adult patients aged 21 years or older with sepsis admitted to the Intensive Care Unit (ICU).

The main questions it aims to answer are:

Does adding Ruta C or vitamin C alone to standard sepsis treatment reduce the length of ICU stay compared with standard sepsis treatment alone?

Do these adjunctive therapies improve clinical outcomes, including 28-day mortality, organ dysfunction, development of septic shock, and the need for mechanical ventilation or vasopressor support?

Do these treatments reduce inflammatory and oxidative stress markers, including interleukin-6 (IL-6), malondialdehyde (MDA), C-reactive protein (CRP), and total leukocytic count?

Researchers will compare three groups to evaluate whether Ruta C provides additional clinical benefits compared with vitamin C alone or standard sepsis care.

A total of 72 patients with sepsis will be randomly assigned in a 1:1:1 ratio to one of three groups:

Group A (Ruta C): Participants will receive oral Ruta C tablets containing rutin 60 mg and vitamin C 160 mg, three times daily, in addition to standard sepsis treatment.

Group B (Vitamin C): Participants will receive oral vitamin C 500 mg once daily, in addition to standard sepsis treatment.

Group C (Control): Participants will receive standard ICU sepsis treatment alone.

Study medications will be administered until ICU discharge, death, or development of septic shock.

Participants will:

Undergo baseline clinical assessments, including APACHE II and SOFA scores, medical history, and demographic data.

Have their SOFA scores assessed at baseline, Day 3, Day 7, and every three days thereafter until ICU discharge or death.

Undergo blood sampling of approximately 10 mL on Days 1 and 7 (approximately 20 mL in total) to measure IL-6 and MDA.

Undergo routine laboratory investigations, including kidney function, liver function, electrolytes, and complete blood count. CRP will be measured on Days 1, 3, and 7, and every three days thereafter until discharge or death.

Be monitored for vital signs, mechanical ventilation requirements, vasopressor use, septic shock development, ICU and hospital length of stay, and adverse events.

Have in-hospital and 28-day mortality outcomes recorded.
primary_outcomes: To evaluate the impact of Ruta C (rutin in combination with vitamin C) or vitamin C alone on length of ICU stay.
title: Effect of Rutin and Vitamin C on Outcomes in Adults With Sepsis Admitted to the Intensive Care Unit

brief_summary: Improving morning strength and cognitive performance using caffeine or whole-body vibration.
primary_outcomes: Bench press and back squat Peak VELOCITY
title: Improving Morning Strength and Cognitive Performance Using Caffeine or Whole-body Vibration.

brief_summary:
Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is a common sleep disorder associated with cardiovascular, metabolic, and neurocognitive complications. The standard diagnostic test for OSA is in-laboratory polysomnography (PSG), which can be costly, labor-intensive, and inconvenient for repeated or large-scale screening. Therefore, there is a need for a convenient and non-invasive method to help identify individuals who may be at risk for OSA.

This prospective observational study aims to develop and clinically validate a multimodal deep learning model that integrates peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO₂) signals and ballistocardiography (BCG) data collected using a smart mattress system to estimate the apnea-hypopnea index (AHI). Adult participants undergoing routine overnight PSG for suspected OSA will be enrolled. During sleep, synchronized SpO₂ and BCG signals will be recorded non-invasively.

The performance of the deep learning model will be evaluated by comparing the predicted AHI values with AHI values derived from PSG. This study seeks to evaluate whether this practical, non-invasive, and scalable approach may support early identification of OSA risk and improve access to sleep disorder assessment in both clinical and home-based settings.
primary_outcomes: Mean absolute error of apnea-hypopnea index estimation
title: Development and Validation of a Multimodal Deep Learning Model Using Peripheral Oxygen Saturation and Ballistocardiography Signals for Predicting Apnea-Hypopnea Index in Obstructive Sleep Apnea

brief_summary: Conventional oral iron supplements often cause gastrointestinal side effects and are limited by poor bioavailability, leaving unabsorbed iron to reach the colon. Hydrocolloid-based hydrogel matrix formulations designed for gradual iron release present a promising approach to improve iron absorption. This study evaluates fractional iron absorption (FIA) from three low-dose hydrogel formulations containing ferrous fumarate compared with ferrous fumarate without a hydrogel matrix. Test products will be administered with water, with and without a standardized breakfast. All formulations will be intrinsically labelled with stable iron isotopes ( 57Fe or 54Fe), and FIA will be determined 14 days after administration based on erythrocyte iron incorporation. In this randomized, within-subject corssover study conducted in non-anemic, iron-depleted women, each participant will receive all test conditions and serve as her own control.
title: Iron Absorption From a Nutritional Iron Supplement

brief_summary:
The goal of the Phase III clinical trial is to evaluate whether using a biological mesh helps improve the efficacy and safety of alimentary tract reconstruction surgery. In digestive surgery, bleeding or leakage at the surgical connection (anastomosis) remains a significant clinical challenge. This study explores whether reinforcing the anastomosis with a biological mesh can effectively reduce these risks and significantly enhance the reliability of the surgical procedure.

The main objectives of this study are:

To evaluate the effectiveness of the biological mesh in reducing bleeding points at the surgical site during the procedure.

To assess the role of the mesh in lowering the risk of postoperative complications, such as anastomotic leaks or stenosis, within 90 days after surgery.

Study Groups:

Experimental Group: Participants who undergo alimentary tract reconstruction with biological mesh reinforcement during surgery.

Control Group: Participants who undergo conventional surgical procedures without the use of mesh.

Participant Flow:

Participants will undergo a health evaluation before surgery to confirm they meet the study criteria. Following the procedure, participants will receive standard postoperative care and return for follow-up clinic visits 30 and 90 days after surgery to monitor their recovery.
primary_outcomes: Number of bleeding points per unit length
title: Prospective, Multicenter, Randomized Controlled Phase III Trial of Biological Mesh for Alimentary Tract Reconstruction in Digestive Surgery

brief_summary: This study investigated whether applying an 8% capsaicin patch to the skin at a planned trocar incision site before abdominal laparoscopic surgery changes postoperative pain and pain sensitivity. Adults were randomly assigned to continued capsaicin treatment or a vehicle control patch after both groups received a brief initial capsaicin application to support blinding. The main comparison was pain in response to standardized pinprick stimuli on the first day after surgery. Other assessments included clinical pain, pain medicine use, mechanical, heat, pressure and electrical sensitivity, endogenous pain modulation, and skin nerve fibers. Telephone follow-up was performed at 1, 2 and 6 months after surgery.
primary_outcomes: Mechanical pain sensitivity around the incision on postoperative day 1
title: Preoperative Capsaicin Patch Treatment to Reduce Pain and Pain Sensitivity After Surgery

brief_summary:
This study examines how people who have had anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) move their legs during walking and stair negotiation, and whether a single session of vibration changes how they ascend and descend stairs.

Participants with ACLR (1 to 3 years after surgery) complete three laboratory visits. At the first visit, they complete walking, stair negotiation, muscle strength, hopping tests, and questionnaires, and stair negotiation is measured before and after a control condition without vibration. At the second and third visits, they receive whole-body vibration (standing on a vibrating platform) or local muscle vibration (a device placed over the thigh muscle) in a counterbalanced order, and stair negotiation is measured before and after each vibration session. Healthy participants matched by sex, age, and activity level complete one visit with the same tests as the first ACLR visit, for comparison.
lead_sponsor: University of North Carolina, Chapel Hill
title: Stair Biomechanics and Vibration Study After ACLR

brief_summary: This study will examine the effectiveness and implementation of a physical activity and health education intervention by comparing outcomes of participants in the intervention group to those in a control group.
primary_outcomes: Lower Extremity Leg Strength Using Sit-to-Stand
title: Adapting an Evidence-Based Physical Activity Intervention to Prevent Frailty and Functional Decline in Older Women Living With HIV

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled study aims to evaluate the effects of a newly developed episiotomy repair simulator using biological tissue and simulated active bleeding on midwifery students' self-efficacy and anxiety levels.

Midwifery students enrolled in the Normal Birth and Postpartum Period course at Sakarya University will be randomly assigned to one of two groups. Both groups will receive the same theoretical training on episiotomy and its repair. Students in the intervention group will practice using the newly developed simulator, which provides a restricted working area and simulated active bleeding conditions. Students in the control group will practice using the traditional beef tongue model.

Students' episiotomy self-efficacy and state anxiety levels will be assessed before and after the training using validated measurement tools. The study aims to determine whether the newly developed simulator offers educational benefits compared with the traditional training method.
primary_outcomes: Change in Episiotomy Self-Efficacy Scale Score
Change in State Anxiety Inventory (STAI-State) Score
title: Effect of a Novel Episiotomy Repair Simulator on Midwifery Students' Self-Efficacy and Anxiety

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether negative pressure wound therapy (NPWT, also called vacuum-assisted closure) works better than direct skin closure for treating burst abdomen in adults. Burst abdomen is a serious complication of abdominal surgery in which the layers of the abdominal wall separate after the operation.

The main question it aims to answer is:

\- Does NPWT increase the number of patients whose abdominal wall muscle layer (fascia) can be fully closed?

Researchers also compared the two treatments for pressure inside the abdomen, length of hospital stay, time and number of sessions needed to close the wound, wound infection, bowel fistula, incisional hernia, need for another operation, and death.

Participants with burst abdomen after elective or emergency abdominal surgery were randomly assigned to one of two treatments:

* NPWT: a foam dressing sealed with a film and connected to a suction pump, changed every 3 days in the operating room until the fascia could be closed.
* Direct skin closure: the skin edges were stitched together over the opened abdominal wall, with dressings changed every other day.

Participants were followed in hospital and then seen in the outpatient clinic 1 month and 3 months after treatment.
title: Negative Pressure Wound Therapy Versus Direct Skin Closure for Burst Abdomen

brief_summary:
The REDUCE study will evaluate whether referral to a comprehensive opioid management program improves breathing stability during sleep in adults with chronic opioid use and sleep-disordered breathing.

This is a Phase II, single-center, randomized, controlled study. Participants will be randomly assigned to either usual care or referral to the UC San Diego Opioid Management Program. Participants referred to the program will receive individualized opioid and pain management from their treating clinician or designated opioid management provider. Treatment may include changes to opioid medications and other pain-management strategies when clinically appropriate. The research team will not prescribe opioids or direct opioid dose adjustments, and no opioid dose reductions are required by the study.

Participants will be followed for approximately 26 weeks. Study assessments will include overnight sleep studies, questionnaires, blood collection, psychomotor vigilance testing, and regular safety monitoring.

The primary objective is to determine whether comprehensive opioid management improves ventilatory stability compared with usual care.
title: Comprehensive Opioid Management and Breathing During Sleep

brief_summary: The aim of this study is to investigate whether the use of larynGuide™ provides accurate and reliable information regarding the position of the endotracheal tube following an intubation attempt in children. larynGuide™ is a software tool that runs on a video laryngoscope platform to assist with laryngoscopy and intubation.
lead_sponsor: Insel Gruppe AG, University Hospital Bern
primary_outcomes: Rate of correct assessment given by larynGuide™
title: AI-assisted Tracheal Intubation in Children

brief_summary: to assess the impact of a modern continuous cryotherapy device on pain intensity and postoperative analgesic consumption in patients undergoing arthroscopic rotator cuff repair.
title: Cryotherapy in Arthroscopic Rotator Cuff Repair

brief_summary: This study looks at how strong the knee muscles are in adolescent athletes and how this strength relates to short-term, high-intensity (anaerobic) performance. Strong, well-balanced thigh muscles may help athletes produce more power during sport movements, but this has not been studied well in teenagers. Male athletes aged 15-16 years will be measured on two separate days. On the first day, their height and body weight will be measured and the strength of the muscles at the front (quadriceps) and back (hamstrings) of both thighs will be tested on a special strength-testing machine. On the second day, they will do a 30-second all-out cycling test to measure anaerobic power. The study will compare the right and left legs and will examine whether knee muscle strength and the balance between the front and back thigh muscles are linked to power output during the cycling test. No treatment or intervention will be given. The results may help coaches and sports scientists understand the physical development of adolescent athletes.
primary_outcomes: Isokinetic Peak Torque of the Knee Extensors and Flexors
title: Isokinetic Knee Strength, Bilateral Muscle Balance, and Anaerobic Performance in Adolescent Athletes

brief_summary: This prospective, randomized, double-blind, controlled clinical trial will evaluate whether adding magnesium sulfate to dexamethasone-augmented ultrasound-guided pectoral nerve block improves postoperative recovery and analgesia in female patients undergoing elective modified radical mastectomy under general anesthesia. Fifty-four participants will be allocated to two groups. Both groups will receive bupivacaine and dexamethasone for PECS block; the intervention group will additionally receive magnesium sulfate. The primary outcome will be the Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15) score at 24 hours after surgery. Secondary outcomes will include postoperative pain scores, opioid consumption, time to first rescue analgesia, postoperative nausea and vomiting, patient satisfaction, block-related complications, intraoperative fentanyl requirements, hemodynamic parameters, and chronic post-mastectomy pain assessed through six months.
primary_outcomes: Quality of Recovery-15 score at 24 hours after surgery
title: Effect of Pectoral Nerve Block (PECS) Using Magnesium Sulfate Added to Dexamethasone on Quality of Recovery and Chronic Post-Mastectomy Pain

brief_summary:
Spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (SBP) is a serious infection that occurs in patients with liver cirrhosis and ascites and is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Current clinical practice often includes follow-up paracentesis approximately 48 hours after starting antibiotic treatment to assess the change in the ascitic fluid polymorphonuclear leukocyte (PMN) count. However, it remains uncertain whether routine follow-up paracentesis improves clinical outcomes compared with a strategy based primarily on clinical response.

This pilot randomized controlled trial will evaluate whether routine follow-up paracentesis is necessary in patients with cirrhosis and SBP. A total of 40 adult patients with SBP will be randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to either a routine follow-up paracentesis group or a no-routine follow-up paracentesis group. All participants will receive standard antibiotic therapy and intravenous albumin according to the study protocol.

Participants assigned to the routine follow-up paracentesis group will undergo repeat paracentesis approximately 48 hours after initiation of antibiotic therapy. Ascitic fluid PMN counts and other laboratory findings will be assessed, and antibiotic treatment may be modified according to the treatment response. Participants assigned to the no-routine follow-up paracentesis group will be monitored using clinical symptoms, vital signs, and blood inflammatory markers without scheduled repeat paracentesis. However, paracentesis may be performed at any time if clinically indicated, such as in the presence of worsening abdominal symptoms, persistent fever, or hemodynamic instability.

The study will compare clinical outcomes between the two treatment strategies, including 30-day and 90-day survival, treatment response, duration of antibiotic therapy, length of hospital stay, SBP recurrence, complications, new infections, and medical costs. The results of this pilot study are intended to provide preliminary evidence for determining whether routine follow-up paracentesis can be safely avoided in selected patients with SBP and to inform the design of a larger randomized controlled trial.
title: Optimal Treatment Strategy for Spontaneous Bacterial Peritonitis

brief_summary: This study is a multi-center, prospective, single-arm clinical trial, with 50 participants expected to take part in it. The primary objective of this study is to assess the efficacy and safety of a conditioning regimen comprising thiotepa combined with TBI, fludarabine, and etoposide for allo-HSCT in patients with R/R acute leukemia or those at high risk for such disease. The secondary objective is to explore the prognosis and benefits for different subgroups of patients with acute leukemia, taking into account their clinical characteristics.
primary_outcomes: One-Year Disease-Free Survival Rate After Allogeneic Transplantation

brief_summary: This single-centre, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2 trial investigates whether lowering cortisol with osilodrostat improves blood-glucose control in adults with mild autonomous cortisol secretion (MACS) and difficult-to-control type 2 diabetes. Forty-four participants are randomly assigned 1:1 to osilodrostat or matching placebo, taken once daily for 12 weeks, together with a blinded hydrocortisone/placebo for stress (sick-day) dosing. The primary outcome is the change in HbA1c from baseline to week 12; secondary outcomes include continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) metrics, cardiometabolic parameters, cortisol measures and quality of life. Participants are followed for a safety visit 4 weeks after the end of treatment.

brief_summary:
Fibromyalgia is a chronic condition characterized by widespread pain, fatigue, sleep disturbances, and difficulties with daily activities. Many people with fibromyalgia also experience psychiatric disorders, particularly depression and anxiety. However, the relationship between these conditions and long-term disability remains incompletely understood.

This nationwide study examines the relationship between fibromyalgia, psychiatric disorders, and disability among individuals whose claims were evaluated by the Israeli National Insurance system between 2018 and 2025.

The study compares two groups: individuals assessed through the general disability system and those assessed through the occupational injury system. It investigates differences between women and men, psychiatric comorbidity, assigned disability severity, temporary and permanent disability, and changes over time.

The research uses existing anonymized administrative records. No experimental treatment, additional examinations, or direct patient participation is required.

The findings may help improve understanding of psychiatric comorbidity in fibromyalgia and support more comprehensive clinical and occupational disability assessments.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Fibromyalgia Patients With Documented Psychiatric Comorbidity
title: Concomitant Fibromyalgia and Psychiatric Disorders

brief_summary: This study looks at the results of a new technique called knife-assisted full-thickness resection (kFTR) for removing rectal lesions. In kFTR, a doctor uses an electrical knife to remove a rectal growth along with the full thickness of the rectal wall. Current methods for removing early rectal tumors each have limits depending on the size and location of the growth. This study collects data from hospitals in multiple countries to find out how well kFTR works and how safe it is. Researchers review medical records and endoscopy reports from patients who already had kFTR at participating hospitals. The main measures are whether the procedure was completed successfully, whether the growth was removed in one piece, whether the edges were cancer-free, and how often complications occurred. The study also tracks hospital stay length, need for additional surgery, cancer recurrence, and death.
title: Outcomes of Knife-Assisted Full-Thickness Resection for Rectal Lesions: A Multicenter Study

brief_summary:
Chronic fatigue that cannot be explained by ongoing exertion or alleviated by rest is characterized by disabling fatigue accompanied with symptoms like pain, sleep problems, cognitive difficulties and more. This type of chronic fatigue is a global health challenge, affecting many individuals in the adult and the adolescent populations. For adolescents, the symptoms may have detrimental effects on school functioning and social participation during a developmental period marked by pivotal maturation. Thus, providing effective treatment for this condition is highly warranted.

The primary objective of the study is to determine whether MBRT given to adolescents with chronic fatigue can reduce fatigue, compared with CAU. Primary outcome is the evaluation of fatigue symptoms on the Chalder Fatigue Questionnaire (CFQ). Secondary objectives are to determine intervention effects on health-related quality of life, pain, school attendance, physical- and social functioning, anxiety, depression and sleep (see Table 1). Other objectives comprise factors that might influence the treatment, like the adolescents' level of neuroticism and self-efficacy, and the parents' level of health anxiety by proxy. In addition, qualitative interviews will be conducted with a subset of participants who have received MBRT, to explore their experiences of the intervention, perceived helpfulness, and what they believe contributed to any changes they may have experienced.

The study is a randomized controlled trial where MBRT for adolescents is compared with CAU (Figure 1). Eligible participants are adolescents aged 12 to 18 years with chronic fatigue lasting six months or more, accompanied by a level of functional impairment that significantly limits their ability to engage in normal social, recreational or educational activities.

Participants will be recruited through referrals from general practitioners and hospital services to either Akershus University Hospital or Oslo University Hospital. At the hospital, all referred patients will go through a screening assessment, which includes clinical examination and blood sampling. This screening assessment will be conducted during the same symptom presentation as at baseline (T1). The physician will decide whether more examinations are needed for a proper clinical assessment. With the test results at hand, the physician will evaluate the predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria. All eligible patients will be contacted and a total of 210 patients will be enrolled. Included participants will complete a questionnaire and be randomized to either MBRT or CAU, this will be regarded as the official baseline (T1). For the participants, MBRT consists of an initial session with a physician for a brief intervention, followed by 4 to 6 sessions with a psychologist or psychiatrist. The adolescent's parents participate in the brief intervention and are also offered an individual session with the psychologist or psychiatrist. The sessions are scheduled close together in time to build and maintain therapeutic momentum. This is followed by a pause of approximately four weeks before the booster session. Primary endpoint assessment is at three months (T2). Total follow-up period is six months (T3). The qualitative interviews with a strategically selected subset of participants who have received MBRT will be conducted after T2. Interviews will take place at Oslo University Hospital, digitally, or by telephone. Recruitment for the interviews will begin once half of the total study sample has been enrolled. At that point, all participants randomized to the MBRT arm will be invited to take part in the qualitative study and a separate informed consent will be obtained. Using a purposive sampling approach to capture variation in age, gender, and treatment response, interviews will continue until approximately 20 adolescents and their parents have been interviewed.
title: Mind Body Reprogramming Therapy for Adolescents With Chronic Fatigue

brief_summary:
Some children's short-sightedness (myopia) continues to worsen despite treatments such as atropine eye drops, myopia-control spectacles or contact lenses. These children may be at greater risk of developing severe short-sightedness and related eye problems later in life.

The BRIGHT-LIGHT study will assess the safety of repeated low-level red-light therapy and explore whether it can slow worsening short-sightedness in children whose myopia is inadequately controlled by conventional treatment. This therapy uses a device that delivers low-power red light to the eyes during short treatment sessions.

Forty children aged 8-16 years will be followed for 12 months: 30 receiving red-light therapy and 10 continuing conventional myopia treatment. Group assignment will depend on the willingness of children and their parents or guardians to start red-light therapy, rather than random allocation.

The main focus is safety, assessed through vision tests, detailed eye scans and tests of retinal function. The study will also assess changes in eye length and spectacle prescription to explore the treatment's effect on myopia progression.
title: BRIGHT-LIGHT: Studying Red Light Therapy for Severe Short-Sightedness or Short-Sightedness That Worsens Despite Standard Treatment

brief_summary:
The goal of this observational study is to learn whether changes in sleep can help identify early signs of relapse in adults with schizophrenia or bipolar disorder. A relapse means that symptoms return or get worse after a stable period.

The study will include 30 adults: 15 with schizophrenia and 15 with bipolar disorder. Participants will have been stable for at least six months and will receive their usual treatment.

The main questions are:

* Are changes in sleep linked to early signs of relapse?
* Are changes in sleep linked to difficulties with everyday activities?

Participants will take part for six months. They will:

* Sleep at home on a thin mattress topper containing sensors that record sleep patterns.
* Meet with a mental health professional at the start and monthly during follow-up.
* Answer questions about symptoms, everyday activities, stressful life events, and usual medicines.
* Have an additional assessment if the device detects specific changes in sleep or time spent in bed over two consecutive nights.

Researchers will compare sleep recordings with symptom assessments to explore whether sleep changes could serve as early warning signs of relapse.
primary_outcomes: Association Between Changes in Sleep duration and Early Relapse Symptoms
title: Sleep Monitoring for Early Detection of Relapse in People With Schizophrenia or Bipolar Disorder Receiving Usual Treatment

brief_summary:
Biktarvy® is a widely prescribed antiretroviral (ARV) medication used for the treatment of HIV-1, formulated as a single-tablet regimen. This combination therapy consists of three potent antiretroviral drugs: bictegravir (BIC/B), an integrase strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI); emtricitabine (FTC/F), a nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NRTI); and tenofovir alafenamide (TAF), the novel prodrug of tenofovir, another NRTI. This tablet (B/F/TAF) is a first-line treatment option recommended by most international guidelines for adults living with HIV. B/F/TAF is widely prescribed due to its high potency, excellent tolerability, and convenient once-daily dosing schedule.

The landscape of HIV management in pregnancy has undergone significant transformation since the mid-1990s. Guidelines for HIV screening during pregnancy, treatment of HIV-positive pregnant individuals, and the use of ARV drugs for prevention of perinatal (vertical) and postnatal HIV transmission have evolved substantially. Current guidelines recommend that pregnant women with HIV receive effective ARV therapy for maternal health and to avoid perinatal transmission; however, recommended treatment options differ in pregnancy due to concerns of toxicity, lower drug exposures, teratogenicity, or lack of information. Recently, pharmacokinetic, efficacy, and teratogenicity data have become available for B/F/TAF when used in pregnancy, and demonstrate consistently that while PK concentrations are lower, viral suppression (VS) is not affected. In response, some guidelines now list B/F/TAF as an alternative regimen to be used in pregnancy but recognize that data are still limited to make this a preferred regimen. French guidelines however, take a more conservative approach, listing BIC among drugs to avoid during pregnancy due to insufficient safety data.

Research question and objectives This retrospective multicentric, multinational observational cohort study is conducted in two distinct parts to evaluate B/F/TAF use in pregnant women with HIV-1.

Part 1: Aims to describe the patterns of B/F/TAF use in women with HIV-1 who received B/F/TAF for at least 30 days at any point during pregnancy. This will be a descriptive analysis of initiation and switch patterns among those exposed to B/F/TAF during pregnancy, and demographics/immunological/clinical characteristics. The reasons for switching B/F/TAF to other ARV treatments during pregnancy will be explored.

Part 2: Aims to describe viral, pregnancy and neonatal outcomes in a subset of women already on B/F/TAF treatment at conception with VS at the first trimester of pregnancy, and among those who continued to receive B/F/TAF through delivery, or switched to another regimen.
lead_sponsor: Centre de Recherches et d'Etude sur la Pathologie Tropicale et le Sida
primary_outcomes: Proportion of women already on B/F/TAF treatment at conception
Proportion of women who started B/F/TAF as their first ARV regimen during pregnancy
Proportion of women who switched-off of B/F/TAF during pregnancy
Proportion of women who switched from other regimens to B/F/TAF during pregnancy
Proportion of women who were on B/F/TAF at time of delivery
Proportion of women who switched off B/F/TAF to another ARV regimen during pregnancy
Distribution of subsequent ARV regimens among women who switched from B/F/TAF to another ARV regimen during pregnancy
title: Cohort of Women Living With HIV-1 and Receiving Bictegravir/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir Alafenamide

brief_summary: FTEXES (Functionalized TEXtiles for Electrical Stimulation) is a wearable platform based on sensorized garments (Smart Pants and Smart T-shirt) with integrated textile electrodes for surface electromyography (EMG) recording and functional electrical stimulation (FES). This single-center, open-label, non-randomized study evaluates the usability of the system in a controlled laboratory setting. Fifteen participants (5 healthy adults, 5 patients with neuromotor disability, 5 healthcare professionals) take part in a single 45-60 minute session including donning, system setup, calibration, functional tasks (gait for the lower limb; reaching and grasping for the upper limb), doffing and skin inspection. The quality of EMG signals recorded with textile electrodes is evaluated as a secondary objective. The study has no therapeutic purpose for individual participants.

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether low-intensity focused ultrasound (LIFU) is safe and may help reduce gambling-related symptoms in adults seeking treatment for gambling disorder.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

* Is LIFU safe and well tolerated in adults with gambling disorder?
* Does LIFU reduce gambling behavior compared with a sham (inactive) procedure?

Researchers will compare participants who receive active LIFU with participants who receive sham LIFU to see whether active treatment leads to greater reductions in gambling behavior.

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned to receive either active LIFU or sham LIFU.
* Receive nine treatment sessions delivered over three treatment days within a five-day period.
* Participate in weekly telehealth cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT).
* Complete assessments of gambling behavior, gambling urges, mood, and quality of life.
* Attend follow-up visits for up to 90 days after active LIFU treatment.

Low-intensity focused ultrasound is a noninvasive technique that uses focused sound waves to influence brain activity. Researchers believe this approach may affect brain circuits involved in reward, cravings, and decision-making that contribute to gambling disorder.

brief_summary: Many people who have major planned surgery for abdominal cancer develop complications afterwards, which can prolong hospital stay and slow recovery. This study tests whether a four-week program led by a trained oncology nurse, started before surgery, reduces these complications. The program combines supervised and home exercise (walking, resistance and breathing exercises), nutrition counseling with protein targets and supplements when needed, education and relaxation techniques to reduce anxiety, and advice on stopping smoking and alcohol. Adults at one hospital will be randomly assigned, in equal numbers, to the program plus usual care or to usual care alone; 104 participants are planned. The main outcome is the Comprehensive Complication Index, a score from 0 to 100 that combines all complications within 30 days after surgery, graded by an assessor who does not know the group. Other outcomes include serious complications, distance walked in six minutes, quality of life, length of hospital stay, hospital readmission, time to first getting out of bed, and adherence to the program. In a qualitative part, 12 to 15 participants from the program group will be interviewed about their experiences, barriers and acceptability. Results from both parts will be combined to interpret the findings.
title: Nurse-Led Prehabilitation Before Major Abdominal Cancer Surgery

brief_summary:
The purpose of this prospective, single-arm pilot feasibility study is to evaluate the safety, feasibility, and preliminary functional outcomes of combining transcutaneous spinal cord stimulation (TSS), dalfampridine (4-aminopyridine), and intensive rehabilitation in adults with chronic spinal cord injury (SCI).

The primary research question is whether this combined treatment approach can be safely and feasibly implemented in an outpatient neurorehabilitation setting. The study will also explore whether participants demonstrate improvements in upper and lower extremity motor function, muscle strength, walking ability, balance, and functional mobility following the intervention.

Eight adults with chronic spinal cord injury will participate in a 12-week rehabilitation program at TRYAbility NeuroRecovery Center. Participants will attend approximately three treatment sessions per week, consisting of 60 minutes of physical therapy and 60 minutes of occupational therapy combined with noninvasive transcutaneous spinal cord stimulation using the ANEUVO ExaStim Stimulation System. All participants will be receiving dalfampridine prescribed by their treating physicians as part of routine medical care. The research team will not prescribe, administer, or adjust medication dosages.

The primary outcomes will focus on participant recruitment, treatment attendance, intervention tolerability, and adverse events to assess the feasibility and safety of the combined approach. Secondary exploratory outcomes will examine changes in upper extremity motor function, hand dexterity, walking speed, walking endurance, balance, and functional mobility.

Participants will undergo standardized clinical assessments at baseline, week 6, and week 12 to evaluate changes in functional performance over time.

The findings will provide preliminary evidence regarding the feasibility, safety, and potential functional benefits of integrating spinal cord stimulation, physician-prescribed dalfampridine, and intensive rehabilitation. Results will help inform the design of larger controlled clinical trials investigating combined treatment approaches for motor recovery following chronic spinal cord injury.

brief_summary:
Compulsive eating behaviors represent a significant issue across various disorders such as Parkinson's disease, bipolar disorders, and obesity.

Despite their apparent differences, these conditions share common underlying disturbances involving the brain's reward system, particularly within dopaminergic networks.6,7 Previous neuroimaging studies have consistently reported reward system connectivity impairment associated with compulsive eating, in each of these disorders. However, few studies have simultaneously explored the neurobiological similarities and specificities of this common symptom, eating behavior, when occurring in different populations and disorders.

The Bi-POTATOS project proposes an original and innovative approach by adopting a transdiagnostic perspective, employing brain imaging and comprehensive psycho-behavioral assessments to investigate common behavioral characteristics and neural circuit alterations associated with compulsive eating across these three conditions. For the first time, this study will allow a direct comparison of the cerebral signatures linked to compulsive eating behavior, clearly distinguishing between transdiagnostic vulnerabilities and features unique to each clinical condition.

The central hypothesis is that similar dysfunctions in brain regions involved in motivation and impulsive decision-making underpin compulsive eating behaviors, irrespective of the initial diagnosis. However, the underlying pathology may modulate these mechanisms, introducing certain specificities.

By clarifying these common mechanisms, the Bi-POTATOS project will not only enhance our understanding of the neurobiological etiology of these disorders but also pave the way for innovative, targeted therapeutic interventions. This project will precisely identify whether specific neural alterations constitute a universally relevant therapeutic target, or conversely, determine which alterations necessitate tailored therapeutic strategies based on the underlying pathology.
interventions: MRI/ MRS (Magnetic Resonance Imaging /Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy)
primary_outcomes: Assessment of resting state seed-based functional connectivity from the limbic striatum (seed: ventral striatum) by MRI.
title: Compulsive Eating and Brain's Reward System in Different Pathologies

The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether the Zeen Mobility Device can improve mobility and function during outpatient rehabilitation for adults with mobility impairments. The study will also evaluate the safety of the device and how easy it is for participants and therapists to use during routine therapy.

The main questions it aims to answer are:

brief_summary:
Retinal arterial macroaneurysm (RAM) is an acquired dilatation of a retinal arteriole that can rupture or leak, causing hemorrhage, exudation, macular edema, and vision loss. No standardized treatment exists, and options range from observation to laser photocoagulation, anti-VEGF therapy, or both.

Laser photocoagulation closes the aneurysm directly and stops leakage. It risks vascular occlusion, temporary worsening of exudate, and scotomas, especially in an actively leaking or edematous macula.

Anti-VEGF therapy reduces vascular permeability and exudation, improving visual acuity and central macular thickness. It does not reliably close the aneurysm itself.

High-dose aflibercept 8 mg has outperformed aflibercept 2 mg in fluid resolution, durability, and dosing interval length in neovascular AMD and diabetic macular edema (PULSAR and PHOTON trials). Its role in RAM-related macular edema, particularly as a pre-laser step to reduce edema and inflammation, has not been studied.

Study rationale: The study will test whether three monthly aflibercept 8 mg loading injections followed by targeted laser to the leaking RAM is a more effective, safer, and more durable sequential strategy than either treatment alone.

primary_outcomes: Change in central macular thickness (CMT), measured by spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SD-OCT), from baseline to the final follow-up visit following sequential aflibercept 8 mg loading doses and laser photocoagulation
title: Efficacy of Aflibercept (8 mg) With Sequential Laser Photocoagulation for Macular Edema Secondary to Retinal Artery Macroaneurysm: Retrospective Study"

The main questions it aims to answer are: Does high-intensity laser therapy improve pain intensity, quality of life, hip range of motion, and global rating of change in patients with Femoroacetabular Impingement Syndrome? Does adding high-intensity laser therapy to exercise therapy produce greater improvements in pain intensity, quality of life, hip range of motion, and global rating of change in patients with Femoroacetabular Impingement Syndrome?

Participants will be randomly assigned to one of two groups for comparison. The first group (control group) will receive a standardized exercise therapy program consistent with routine exercises for femoroacetabular impingement syndrome, along with sham high-intensity laser therapy. The second group (experimental group) will receive the same standardized exercise therapy program in addition to active high-intensity laser therapy.
title: The Effectiveness of High-intensity Laser Therapy in Femoroacetabular Impingement Syndrome

This pilot randomized controlled trial will recruit 40 women who were identified as being at high risk for preeclampsia during pregnancy and subsequently developed a hypertensive disorder of pregnancy. Participants will be enrolled 6 to 8 weeks after delivery and randomly assigned to a 12-week exercise program or standard postnatal care. The exercise program will consist of three sessions per week combining moderate-intensity aerobic exercise, resistance training, and pelvic floor exercises.

Cardiovascular function, blood pressure, blood markers of cardiometabolic health, physical fitness, and body composition will be assessed before and after the 12-week period. Changes in mood, sleep quality, and health-related quality of life will also be evaluated. The study will provide preliminary evidence on the effects of postpartum exercise in this population and inform the design of a larger trial.

Researchers will compare a higher-force IASTM treatment to a lower-force IASTM treatment to determine whether force dose influences physical and patient-reported outcomes.

Participants will:

Attend two study visits separated by a washout period of 3-7 days. Receive a lower-force IASTM treatment during one visit and a higher-force IASTM treatment during the other visit, in a randomly assigned order.

Complete questionnaires about expectations, anxiety, treatment comfort, and treatment experience.

Undergo assessments of ankle flexibility, calf muscle stiffness, sensitivity to pressure, walking speed, and lower-body performance before and after each treatment session.

The findings from this study will help researchers better understand how biomechanical and non-biomechanical factors contribute to the effects of soft tissue treatments and may help inform the development of more effective rehabilitation interventions.

brief_summary:
Boutonnière injuries involve damage to the central slip of the extensor tendon over the proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joint (zone III) of the finger. These injuries disrupt the balance of the extensor mechanism, leading to volar displacement of the lateral bands and progressive development of Boutonnière deformity, characterized by PIP joint flexion and distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint hyperextension. Due to the gradual onset and closed nature of the injury, diagnosis is often delayed, and untreated cases may result in joint contractures, reduced range of motion (ROM), pain, and functional limitations.

Treatment is typically conservative and requires prolonged immobilization and splinting, often followed by dynamic orthoses such as Capener splints. However, evidence supporting current treatment strategies is limited and clinical outcomes are variable. Recently, the Relative Motion Flexion (RMF) orthosis has been introduced as an alternative approach aimed at restoring extensor mechanism balance. Existing evidence is limited to small or heterogeneous studies, highlighting the need for further evaluation.

This pilot study aims to assess the feasibility and preliminary effects of RMF orthosis treatment in patients with Boutonnière injuries. The primary objective is to evaluate changes in finger range of motion (ROM) and to estimate variability and within-subject correlations to inform sample size calculations for a future randomized controlled trial. Additional feasibility outcomes include recruitment rate, adherence to treatment, and practicality of measurement procedures.

Secondary objectives include evaluating pain, grip strength, functional hand limitations in daily activities, and patient-reported tolerability and comfort of the orthosis.

The study will be conducted as a prospective longitudinal cohort pilot study with repeated within-subject measurements at baseline, 3 months, and 12 months. A total of 25 adult patients with acute or subacute closed zone III extensor tendon injuries will be recruited consecutively at the Hand Surgery Rehabilitation Unit, Skåne University Hospital, Malmö.

Inclusion criteria include age ≥18 years, positive pencil test, and confirmed central slip injury. Exclusion criteria include open injuries, significant joint contractures (\>20°), chronic injuries (\>1 year), previous surgery or trauma in the same finger, concomitant fractures or tendon/nerve injuries, inflammatory arthropathies, and severe cognitive or psychiatric conditions or substance abuse.

All participants will receive treatment with an RMF orthosis according to a structured protocol consisting of 6 weeks of continuous use followed by 6 weeks of intermittent daytime and nighttime use. No separate control group will be included; analyses will be based on within-subject comparisons over time.

Primary outcome is ROM measured at the MCP, PIP, and DIP joints using a goniometer. Secondary outcomes include pain (Numeric Rating Scale), grip strength (Jamar dynamometer), hand function (QuickDASH), adherence and tolerability questionnaires, and recruitment rate.

Data will be analyzed using descriptive statistics and nonparametric longitudinal methods, including Friedman tests and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests for paired comparisons across time points.

The study will be conducted in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki, with ethical approval sought from the Swedish Ethical Review Authority. All participants will provide informed consent, and data will be pseudonymized in accordance with GDPR. The study poses minimal risk, and participants will be monitored throughout treatment with adjustments made as needed.

This pilot study will generate essential data on treatment variability, feasibility, and preliminary outcomes of RMF orthosis use. The results will inform the design of a future randomized controlled trial and may contribute to improved evidence-based management of Boutonnière injuries, potentially leading to better functional outcomes and more efficient rehabilitation strategies.
interventions: Relative Motion Flexion (RMF) orthosis intervention group
title: Conservative Treatment With Relative Motion Flexion Orthosis for Boutonniere Injuries in Fingers

A total of 35 newborns at risk of encephalopathy will be recruited.

During aEEG monitoring, one type of electrode will be placed on each cerebral hemisphere: on one hemisphere, the standard electrode normally used according to each hospital's protocol, and on the other, the new aCUP-E electrode. This design allows direct comparison under similar conditions to assess recording quality, reliability and ease of use. The multicentre methodology also facilitates a more representative and diverse sample, increasing the robustness and generalisability of the results.

This study seeks to determine whether aCUP-E can replace conventional electrodes, offering a safe and effective alternative that improves the quality of neonatal neurological monitoring and adapts to different clinical contexts.

brief_summary:
The Elephant II represents a second-generation flexible and navigable suction UAS. It is available in different calibers and incorporates a flexible distal segment that facilitates navigation with the ureteroscope. Compared with earlier-generation devices, the second-generation Elephant II incorporates a more flexible tip, an improved water-sealing cap, and an enhanced pressure-control module designed to facilitate more consistent suction without requiring continuous manual thumb control.

The development of the Elephant IV represents a further technological evolution toward intelligent pressure-controlled suction during RIRS. Unlike earlier suction-only systems, the newer generation integrates intrarenal pressure monitoring and automated pressure-control mechanisms, allowing irrigation and suction to be dynamically adjusted according to the measured intrarenal pressure. Such an approach may provide a more standardized and physiologically controlled operative environment, potentially avoiding both excessive intrarenal pressure and unnecessarily aggressive suction.

Therefore, a direct comparison between Elephant II and Elephant IV UASs during RIRS is clinically relevant. Such a study could determine whether the incorporation of real-time intrarenal pressure monitoring and automated pressure regulation translates into measurable improvements in intrarenal pressure control, endoscopic visibility, stone-free rate, irrigation/suction performance, and postoperative infectious and other complications.

The aim of this work is to compare the efficacy and safety of automated intrarenal irrigation during retrograde intrarenal surgery (RIRS) versus the manual hand-operated irrigation.
title: Automated Versus Manual Irrigation During Flexible Ureteroscopy

brief_summary:
Radiotherapy, a cornerstone of comprehensive cancer treatment, relies heavily on clinician expertise for target volume contouring and treatment planning. Consequently, clinical practice is often constrained by procedural bottlenecks, inter-observer variability, and prolonged iterative feedback cycles. Although current artificial intelligence (AI) models have demonstrated progress in automated contouring, key limitations persist, including insufficient integration of multimodal clinical text, a lack of closed-loop dosimetric feedback, and limited generalizability across complex cancer types.

This study aims to develop and validate RATA (Radiotherapy Treatment Multi-Agent Assistant), a novel large model system powered by a collaborative multi-agent architecture. Driven by Large Language Model (LLM) decision engines, RATA processes pathological imaging, electronic health records (EHR), and multimodal medical data to construct a end-to-end, fully automated closed-loop pipeline encompassing "target contouring, plan design, dosimetric evaluation, and reflective refinement." Innovatively breaking through traditional unidirectional radiotherapy workflows, the system establishes a dosimetric feedback-driven adaptive iteration mechanism, leveraging dose distribution outcomes to guide multi-agent dynamic fine-tuning of target volumes, thereby mimicking the collaborative clinical logic between senior radiation oncologists and medical physicists.

For validation, this study adopts a multi-center, three-stage clinical validation framework-comprising multi-center retrospective validation, human-AI collaborative efficacy assessment, and a prospective randomized controlled trial (RCT)-to comprehensively evaluate the system's performance in improving contouring precision, mitigating experience-dependent disparities across clinician seniority, and reducing total workflow processing time. Implementation of the RATA platform holds potential to eliminate redundant operational steps, enabling a minute-level "scan-to-treat" response. Furthermore, its natural language interaction interface optimizes human-AI collaboration and substantially reduces clinical workload. Overall, this study not only establishes a standardized, intelligent assistance paradigm for precision radiation oncology but also provides essential evidence-based support and technological foundations for the clinical translation of multimodal AI in complex cancer management.
title: Automated Radiation Target Contouring and Treatment Planning Via RATA: A Multi-Center RCT

This study will be conducted at the Department of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery, Faculty of Dentistry, Cairo University. It will include patients aged 18-30 years presenting with non-restorable mandibular molars indicated for extraction and delayed implant placement.

Eligible patients will be randomly allocated into two equal groups:

* Group I (Intervention group): Extraction sockets will be filled with locally applied melatonin gel.
* Group II (Control group): Extraction sockets will be filled with placebo gel. All patients will undergo atraumatic tooth extraction under local anesthesia, followed by socket curettage, saline irrigation, application of the allocated gel, collagen membrane coverage, and primary wound closure.

Postoperative care will include standardized medications and oral hygiene instructions. Patients will be followed up clinically and radiographically. CBCT will be used to assess the primary outcome, which is the dimensional change in vertical alveolar bone height (ΔH). At 12 weeks, core biopsy specimens will be obtained for histopathological assessment of bone quality, including newly formed bone, bone maturation, trabecular architecture, and osteoblastic activity.

Sample size: The total sample size will be determined based on the primary outcome (ΔH), using an appropriate statistical power calculation, with equal allocation between the two groups. The final number of participants will be specified according to the statistician's sample size calculation.
