The study included 270 women at a public hospital in eastern Türkiye between September 2020 and March 2021. Participants were divided into three groups of 90 women each.

Women in the hypno-breastfeeding group received guidance on relaxation, positive affirmations, imagination, and visualization during late pregnancy and after childbirth. Women in the oxytocin massage group received two back massage sessions after childbirth. Women in the control group received routine care without either of these additional interventions.

On the first day after childbirth, the researchers assessed breastfeeding motivation, perceived milk supply, mother-to-infant bonding, and uterine recovery to compare the three groups.

brief_summary:
This randomized clinical trial aims to investigate the effects of different intracanal methylene blue agitation techniques used during antimicrobial photodynamic therapy (aPDT) on root canal microbiota, host inflammatory responses, postoperative pain, and periapical healing in previously root canal-treated teeth with asymptomatic apical periodontitis.

A total of 60 participants will be randomly allocated to four groups (15 participants per group): aPDT without additional methylene blue agitation (control), aPDT with standard needle irrigation(SNI), aPDT with passive ultrasonic irrigation (PUI), and aPDT with Er,Cr:YSSG laser-assisted irrigation (LAI).

All participants will undergo nonsurgical root canal retreatment. Methylene blue will be used as the photosensitizing agent, and photodynamic light irradiation will be performed using the LED FotoSan device in all groups.

Root canal samples will be collected at three treatment stages to investigate changes in microbial communities and inflammatory markers. Shotgun metagenomic sequencing will be performed in a subset of participants, while selected inflammatory cytokines will be measured using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA).

Postoperative pain and radiographic periapical healing will also be evaluated during follow-up.

The study aims to determine whether different methylene blue agitation techniques influence the microbiological, inflammatory, and clinical outcomes of antimicrobial photodynamic therapy during root canal retreatment.
primary_outcomes: Postoperative Pain Intensity Assessed Using a Visual Analog Scale (VAS)

brief_summary:
Periodontitis can cause loss of the bone supporting the teeth. Regenerative surgery aims to repair these defects and improve tooth support. Bioactive glass is a synthetic bone graft material used to fill periodontal bone defects. A resorbable collagen membrane may be placed over the graft to support healing, but its additional long-term benefit remains uncertain.

This randomized clinical trial compared bioactive glass alone with bioactive glass covered by a resorbable collagen membrane in 40 participants with periodontal intrabony defects. Both groups underwent surgical cleaning of the defects before placement of the assigned materials. Clinical measurements were performed by an examiner who was unaware of treatment allocation.

Assessments were conducted before surgery, at 6 months, and at approximately 12 years. They included periodontal pocket depth, clinical attachment level, gum recession, plaque and bleeding scores, and defect dimensions measured on dental radiographs. Seventeen participants attended the 12-year examination. The study evaluated whether treatment improvements were maintained over time and whether adding a collagen membrane provided additional benefit.
interventions: Periodontal regenerative surgery with bioactive glass alone
Periodontal regenerative surgery with bioactive glass and a collagen membrane

brief_summary:
This study aims to evaluate the reliability and validity of two Uzbek-language questionnaires in adults with and without primary hypothyroidism (an underactive thyroid).

The SARC-F questionnaire asks about difficulties with everyday physical activities, such as walking, standing up from a chair, and climbing stairs. It helps identify people who may need further assessment for sarcopenia, a condition involving reduced muscle strength and function. The International Physical Activity Questionnaire-Short Form (IPAQ-SF) assesses walking, moderate and vigorous physical activity, and sitting time during the previous seven days.

The study will include 480 Uzbek-speaking adults aged 18 years or older in the Andijan region of Uzbekistan. Of these, 240 will have primary hypothyroidism and 240 will have normal thyroid function. Both women and men will participate.

All participants will complete both questionnaires and undergo measurements of muscle strength and physical function. At least 200 participants will complete the same questionnaires again after 7-14 days.

The researchers will examine how consistently the questionnaires measure physical function and activity and how their results relate to objective functional measurements. No experimental treatment will be provided.

Although clinical guidelines recommend weight loss and regular physical activity as first line treatments this can be difficult for patients to do. This study aims to better understand what makes it harder or easier for patients to participate in weight management or exercise programs and to design a weight and exercise program specifically tailored to older adults managing chronic health issues.

Based on input from patients and providers we will design and pilot a virtual exercise and weight management program to help patients with knee osteoarthritis in their home. Participants will be asked to fill out questionnaires about their knee pain and have phone or video check-ins with the study team to monitor progress.
interventions: Home-based exercise and weight management program

brief_summary:
Postoperative delirium (POD) is a common complication following cardiac surgery and is associated with prolonged intensive care unit (ICU) stay, increased healthcare costs, and adverse clinical outcomes. Fast-track anesthesia aims to facilitate early postoperative extubation and recovery; however, its association with postoperative neurocognitive outcomes remains uncertain.

This single-center, prospective observational cohort study aims to compare the incidence of postoperative delirium between patients undergoing fast-track and conventional postoperative anesthetic management following elective cardiac surgery. The study will be conducted at the Second Affiliated Hospital of Nanchang University from January 2026 to January 2027. A total of 320 adult patients are planned to be enrolled, including 130 in the fast-track group and 190 in the control group.

Patients will be categorized according to the duration of postoperative endotracheal intubation. The fast-track group will include patients extubated within 6 hours after surgery, while the control group will include patients extubated more than 6 hours after surgery. Anesthesia and postoperative care will follow routine clinical practice without study-mandated interventions. The primary outcome is the incidence of postoperative delirium, assessed using the Confusion Assessment Method for the Intensive Care Unit (CAM-ICU) or the 3-Minute Diagnostic Interview for Delirium (3D-CAM) from postoperative day 1 through day 7 or until hospital discharge, whichever occurs first.
lead_sponsor: Second Affiliated Hospital of Nanchang University
title: The Impact of Fast-Track Anesthesia on Postoperative Neurocognitive Function in Patients Undergoing Cardiac Surgery

brief_summary:
The goal of this study is to learn whether a meal program for people with heart failure works well when it is brought to new American Indian and Alaska Native communities, and how it affects patients, their households and local Native food systems. The program provides meals that are both medically tailored and culturally tailored, made with traditional foods from local Native producers. In an earlier randomized trial in Navajo Nation (MUTTON-HF), this program reduced hospitalizations and improved quality of life.

The study will examine whether the program can be successfully implemented at new Indian Health Service and Tribal sites and whether patients and community partners find it acceptable. It will also look at whether taking part improves patients' and caregivers' food security, financial strain, ability to work and other measures of economic stability, and whether the program strengthens local Native food systems by directing purchasing to Native farmers and ranchers and creating jobs.

About 100 adults with heart failure will take part at up to three Indian Health Service or Tribal health facilities. Participants will receive 14 frozen meals each week for 12 weeks, picked up or delivered locally, and will complete surveys when they enroll and again at 3 months. Some will be invited to an interview about their experience. Caregivers, participating farmers and ranchers, and program staff will also be asked to complete surveys and interviews, and health care use will be collected from medical records.

Background: Non-specific low back pain is a leading cause of global disability and physical, psychological, and socioeconomic burdens. While instrument-assisted soft tissue mobilization has shown benefits for pain, disability, and range of motion, it remains unclear whether these effects stem from the instrument itself, mobilization mechanisms, or placebo factors.

Additionally, no prior study has directly compared it with deep friction massage.

Objective: To compare the effects of instrument-assisted soft tissue mobilization, deep friction massage, and sham treatment on pain, disability, lumbar range of motion, pressure pain threshold, psychological status, and electromyographical activation in individuals with non specific low back pain. Methods: This trial will recruit 66 participants aged 18 to 60 years with chronic low back pain.

Participants will be randomly assigned to one of three groups and receive a standardized four week rehabilitation program of two sessions per week, including hot packs, stretching, strengthening. Outcomes will be assessed at baseline, immediately after the first session, and after four weeks using pain intensity scales, disability indices, range of motion measurements, Page 2of 6 surface electromyography as primary outcome measures, and pressure pain thresholds, and psychological status evaluations as secondary. Conclusion: This study will provide evidence on the comparative effectiveness of these interventions, helping clarify the specific therapeutic value of instrument-assisted soft tissue mobilization.
title: Effects of IASTM, Deep Friction Massage, and Sham Instrument-Assisted Soft Tissue Mobilization on Electromyographical Activation, Pain and Function in Non-Specific Low Back Pain

The study includes a Screening Period of up to 28 days (Day -28 to Day -1) for participants in all cohorts. Up to 60 participants are planned to be enrolled in this study, with 12 participants per cohort randomized in a 3:1 ratio to receive RAP-219-LAI or placebo.

brief_summary: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a chronic metabolic disease that may impair exercise capacity, respiratory muscle strength, balance, and quality of life, and increase fatigue. Exercise training is an important component of diabetes management. However, the effects of functional inspiratory muscle training, which combines breathing exercises with functional movements and postural control activities, have not been sufficiently investigated in individuals with T2DM. This study aims to compare the effects of online functional inspiratory muscle training and combined exercise training on functional capacity, fatigue, and balance in individuals with T2DM. The study will also investigate changes in respiratory muscle strength, peripheral muscle strength, quality of life, and activities of daily living. This prospective, single-blind, randomized controlled trial will include 39 individuals aged 40-65 years who have been diagnosed with T2DM. Participants will be randomly assigned to three groups in a 1:1:1 ratio: a combined exercise training group, a functional inspiratory muscle training group, and a control group. Both exercise groups will participate in an eight-week home-based training program consisting of three sessions per week. Two sessions will be supervised online by a physiotherapist, while one session will be performed independently. The combined exercise training group will perform aerobic, resistance, and breathing exercises. The functional inspiratory muscle training group will perform progressive inspiratory muscle training combined with core stabilization, postural control, and functional exercises. The control group will receive physical activity counseling and an informational brochure without participating in a structured exercise intervention. Participants will be evaluated at baseline and after the eight-week intervention. The primary outcomes will be functional capacity, fatigue, and balance, assessed using the Six-Minute Walk Test, Functional Assessment of Chronic Illness Therapy-Fatigue Scale (FACIT-F), Timed Up and Go Test, and the short version of the Activities-specific Balance Confidence Scale. Secondary outcomes will include respiratory and peripheral muscle strength, lower-extremity functional performance, diabetes-related quality of life, instrumental activities of daily living, and anthropometric measurements. This study aims to provide evidence regarding the effectiveness of online functional inspiratory muscle training compared with combined exercise training in improving physical function and balance in individuals with T2DM.
primary_outcomes: Fatigue Level Assessed by FACİT-Fatigue Scale
Dynamic Balance Assessed by Timed Up and Go Test (TUG)
Balance Confidence Assessed by Activities-specific Balance Confidence Scale (ABC)
title: Comparison of Functional Inspiratory Muscle Training and Combined Exercise Training in Individuals With Type 2 Diabetes

This study investigated whether training on a treadmill with two independently moving belts could improve walking symmetry more than conventional treadmill training in older adults recovering from hip fracture surgery.

Twenty-four participants were randomly assigned to either split-belt treadmill training, in which the belt under the fractured leg moved more slowly, or conventional treadmill training, in which both belts moved at the same speed. Participants were scheduled to receive six training sessions over two weeks, in addition to their usual rehabilitation.

Walking symmetry and mobility were assessed at two time points before training, immediately after training, and four weeks later. Additional assessments included walking endurance, walking speed, confidence in maintaining balance, and self-reported physical function.

The study aimed to determine whether split-belt treadmill training could provide additional benefits for walking recovery after hip fracture.

brief_summary:
Background and Rationale Gastric cancer is one of the most common gastrointestinal malignancies worldwide and in Vietnam, ranking among the leading causes of cancer-related mortality. Surgical resection-specifically total gastrectomy-serves as a primary curative treatment for patients with upper- and mid-gastric cancers. However, total gastrectomy leads to severe physiological stress, altered digestive mechanics, loss of gastric capacity, and early postoperative complications such as early satiety, dumping syndrome, and malabsorption.

Consequently, patients undergoing total gastrectomy suffer rapid and severe postoperative weight loss (often exceeding 10% of body weight), progressive skeletal muscle wasting (sarcopenia), depletion of visceral proteins, and severe malnutrition. Postoperative malnutrition is strongly associated with delayed wound healing, higher infection rates, prolonged hospital stays, poorer tolerance to adjuvant chemotherapy, and reduced overall survival. While preoperative and postoperative nutritional interventions are recommended internationally, comprehensive evidence regarding personalized medical nutrition therapy after total gastrectomy in Vietnam remains limited.

Study Objectives

This clinical trial was conducted by investigator Nguyen Thi Thanh Hoa at Vietnam National Cancer Hospital (Tan Trieu campus) in Hanoi, Vietnam, with approval from the Biomedical Research Ethics Committee of Hanoi Medical University (Approval No. 845/GCN-HĐĐĐNCYSH-ĐHYHN). The main objectives of the study were:

* To describe the preoperative nutritional status and related clinical factors in patients undergoing total gastrectomy for gastric cancer at Vietnam National Cancer Hospital.
* To evaluate the efficacy of a specialized perioperative medical nutritional intervention protocol on postoperative nutritional status, body composition, gastrointestinal recovery, and clinical outcomes compared to standard nutritional care.

Study Design \& Intervention Protocols The study was designed as a prospective, controlled clinical trial with pre- and post-intervention comparison. A total of 76 adult patients (aged 20 years or older) with histologically confirmed gastric cancer indicated for total gastrectomy were enrolled and assigned to two equal groups of 38 patients matched by age, gender, cancer stage, and GLIM (Global Leadership Initiative on Malnutrition) baseline nutritional status.

Intervention Group (n = 38): Received an active, comprehensive perioperative medical nutrition protocol developed by the research team.

Days 1-4 Post-Op: Received complete parenteral nutrition providing 25 kcal/kg/day and 1.0 g protein/kg/day containing balanced macronutrients (glucose, amino acids, lipids) alongside essential vitamins and minerals.

Early Enteral Nutrition: Enteral feeding was initiated early (within 24-48 hours postoperatively, even prior to the return of flatus) via nasogastric tube or oral route.

Specialized Formula: Patients were fed a specialized peptide-hydrolyzed medical nutrition formula (combining animal and plant proteins, MCTs, EPA/Omega-3 fatty acids, and immunonutrients including L-Arginine, L-Glutamine, and RNA nucleotides). Each 250 mL package supplied 300 kcal, 16.5 g protein, 7.8 g fat, and 41.0 g carbohydrates.

Post-Discharge Care: Targeted daily energy and protein intakes (minimum 30 kcal/kg/day and 1.0 g protein/kg/day) were maintained for 1 month, supported by weekly telephone nutritional counseling after discharge.

Control Group (n = 38): Received standard postoperative nutritional care practiced at the hospital.

Days 1-2 Post-Op: Received basic intravenous fluids (saline, 5% glucose) and partial parenteral nutrition.

Postoperative Feeding: Oral feeding was delayed until the return of flatus (typically starting with thin rice porridge) without standardized caloric targets or structured immunonutrition supplements.
interventions: Oral Nutritional Supplementation (ONS) and Structured Dietary Counseling
title: Effectiveness Of Nutritional Intervention on Recovery and Clinical Outcomes in Gastric Cancer Patients Undergoing Total Gastrectomy at Vietnam National Cancer Hospital (NUTRIGAST)

brief_summary:

* Is a single intravenous exosome injection safe and well tolerated?

Researchers compared three groups: standard therapy plus a saline (sham) injection, standard therapy plus HWJ-MSC exosomes, and standard therapy plus HWJ-MSC exosomes combined with HUVEC exosomes, to see whether exosome therapy, alone or in combination, improves kidney function and markers of systemic inflammation, fibrosis, oxidative stress, and endothelial dysfunction.

Participants:

* Continued their usual standard CKD treatment
* Returned for a follow-up visit at Day 30 for blood and urine tests and a clinical examination

brief_summary:
Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) is a common condition among young women (the leading endocrine disorder) and is responsible for 70% of anovulatory infertility cases. Clinically, it has been defined since 2003 by the Rotterdam criteria, according to the French College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists. PCOS represents a significant challenge in reproductive medicine, as it is associated with infertility rates ranging from 20% to 74%. Ovarian stimulation is the first-line treatment for PCOS, as no etiological treatment is available. The first-line pharmacological treatment is Clomiphene Citrate. In cases where Clomiphene Citrate fails, the second-line treatment is ovarian drilling. Traditionally, ovarian drilling was performed via laparoscopy or fertiloscopy. Fertiloscopy had the advantage of being quicker and scarless for patients, with reported failure and conversion rates to laparoscopy of 10% to 20% depending on the studies. However, fertiloscopy is no longer practiced due to the discontinuation of the device. With the advent of vNOTES laparoscopy (Vaginal Natural Orifice Transluminal Endoscopic Surgery) in the 2010s for benign gynecological conditions, the possibility of a new vaginal approach for ovarian drilling is now being considered. The Primary Objective is to Evaluate the efficacy of ovarian drilling via vNOTES laparoscopy in terms of resumption of spontaneous ovulatory cycles in PCOS patients requiring surgical treatment.

Study Type:

Single-center, randomized, controlled, two-arm, proof-of-concept study. Number of Centers: 1

Study Description:

During the gynecology consultation, if an indication for ovarian drilling is established, the patient will be invited to participate in the study protocol. The study information sheet, detailing the study procedures and objectives, along with the consent form, will be provided to the patient.

A second consultation with the investigator will be scheduled to address any questions following a reflection period. If the patient consents, both she and the investigator will sign the consent form.

Randomization will be conducted using REDCap® software. The patient will then be assigned to either the vNOTES group or the laparoscopy group. Surgery will be performed by surgeons designated as "experts" in the respective surgical approach. The procedure will follow the standard techniques of the department.

Ovulatory cycle resumption will be assessed 6 months postoperatively during a follow-up consultation.
interventions: Ovarian drilling by vaginal laparoscopy VNotes
primary_outcomes: The resumption (or not) of an ovulatory cycle
title: Efficacy of Ovarian Drilling Via vNOTES Laparoscopy in Patients With PCOS

Clinical Trial Summary

The goal of this clinical trial is to compare the effectiveness of Saccharomyces boulardii CNCM I-745 and multi-strain Bacillus clausii in reducing the frequency of acute watery diarrhea in children aged 6 to 24 months. The main question it aims to answer is:

\- Which probiotic is more effective in reducing the daily frequency of acute watery diarrhea in children?

Researchers will compare Saccharomyces boulardii CNCM I-745 with a four-strain mixture of Bacillus clausii (O/C, SIN, N/R, T) to determine which is more effective in reducing diarrhea frequency.

Participants will:

* Receive either Saccharomyces boulardii CNCM I-745 at a daily dose of 10 billion CFU or multi-strain Bacillus clausii at a daily dose of 4 billion CFU for 3 days.
* Receive standard treatment for diarrhea, including oral rehydration therapy (ORS), zinc supplementation, and dietary advice.
* Be followed for 3 days after admission, with daily recording of the frequency of diarrhea episodes.
title: Comparison of Two Probiotics for Reducing Diarrhea Frequency in Children Aged 6-24 Months

brief_summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to learn whether radiofrequency (a heat-producing electrotherapy applied through an intravaginal electrode and over the abdomen), a supervised pelvic floor and core exercise programme, or both together reduce menstrual pain in women aged 18 to 35 years with primary dysmenorrhea. The main question it aims to answer is: do the three treatments differ in menstrual pain intensity (0-10 visual analogue scale)? Researchers will also compare pain quality, use of painkillers, quality of life, sexual function, premenstrual symptoms, pelvic floor muscle function and satisfaction with treatment, up to 1 year after treatment.

One hundred and twenty women will be randomly assigned to one of three groups:

* Radiofrequency: eight weekly sessions of about 30 minutes.
* Exercise: 16 supervised group sessions of 45 minutes (twice a week for 8 weeks).
* Combined: both treatments. Participants will complete questionnaires, a pain-medication diary and a pelvic floor examination before treatment and 1 week, 6 months and 1 year after treatment.
interventions: Pelvic floor and core exercise programme
title: Radiofrequency and Pelvic Floor Exercise for Primary Dysmenorrhea

brief_summary:
This prospective, randomized controlled study aims to evaluate whether adding femoral and sciatic nerve blocks to obturator nerve block improves the prevention of obturator reflex during transurethral resection of bladder tumors under spinal anesthesia.

Ninety patients will be randomly assigned to three groups: obturator nerve block alone, obturator plus femoral nerve blocks, or obturator plus femoral and sciatic nerve blocks. Adductor muscle contractions, surgeon satisfaction, procedure duration, and complications will be evaluated.
primary_outcomes: Number of Participants With at Least One Intraoperative Adductor Muscle Contraction
title: Femoral and Sciatic Nerve Blocks Added to Obturator Nerve Block for Prevention of Obturator Reflex

brief_summary: in this era, increasing use of smart gadgets such as mobile phones, laptops, computers etc has led to rise in musculoskeletal disorders, particularly Text Neck Syndrome, which is characterized by neck and upper back pain with prolonged neck flexion and forward head posture. Somatic education approaches such as the Alexander Technique and Feldenkrais Method offer alternative strategies by emphasizing postural awareness, movement quality, and neuromuscular re-education rather than repetitive exercise alone. The study will be conducted as a randomized clinical trial and the assessor will be blind. Sample size of 46 subjects will be taken according to inclusion criteria and subjects will be allocated in two groups by computer generator software. Conventional intervention will be received as a standardized treatment protocol in both groups with additional intervention. Group A will receive Alexander technique while Group B will receive Feldenkrais technique. The data will be analyzed using appropriate statistical methods to evaluate the effectiveness of each intervention. This study's results can provide valuable information to healthcare professionals on how to manage Text neck syndrome.
title: Effects of Alexander Technique Versus Feldenkrais Somatic Training in Patients With Text Neck Syndrome

brief_summary: This study aims to evaluate the clinical efficacy and safety of integrated traditional Chinese and Western medicine in the treatment of sepsis, explore its potential value in improving clinical outcomes, and provide high-quality clinical evidence for the integrated management of sepsis.In addition, blood samples will be collected for phenotyping and subsequent transcriptomic, proteomic, and metabolomic analyses.
interventions: Matching Placebo for Syndrome-Differentiated Chinese Herbal Medicine
lead_sponsor: Henan University of Traditional Chinese Medicine
title: Integrated Medicine for Sepsis: An RCT With Phenotyping

brief_summary:
Fasting before surgery does not always ensure that the stomach is empty. Residual gastric contents may be relevant to the risk of stomach contents entering the lungs during anaesthesia.

This multicentre prospective observational study will enrol 240 adults scheduled for elective isolated coronary artery bypass grafting at two hospitals in Türkiye. Gastric ultrasound will be performed before any sedative or anaesthetic medication is administered. The study will determine the proportion of patients with high-risk gastric contents despite routine preoperative fasting.

High-risk gastric contents will be defined as any solid or thick contents, or an estimated clear fluid volume greater than 1.5 mL/kg. Associations with patient characteristics, medical conditions, medication use and fasting duration will also be examined.

The anaesthetist's management plan will be recorded before the ultrasound findings are known. After the findings are communicated, any changes in surgical timing, anaesthetic induction, airway management or aspiration precautions will be documented. Fasting practices will not be modified for research purposes, and all clinical decisions will remain with the attending anaesthetist.
primary_outcomes: Proportion of Participants With High-Risk Gastric Contents on Preoperative Gastric Ultrasound
title: Preoperative Gastric Ultrasound and Anaesthetic Management in Patients Undergoing Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting

brief_summary:
When the nerve inside a tooth becomes inflamed, it can cause severe pain and may eventually lead to the death of the nerve. In these cases, root canal treatment is necessary to remove the inflamed nerve or to treat or prevent infection associated with a dead nerve.

During root canal treatment, the root canals are carefully cleaned and then filled. This is usually done using a flexible, rubber-like material called gutta-percha, combined with a special dental cement known as a root canal sealer.

Different types of root canal sealers are available, including AH Plus and BioRoot Flow. The aim of this study is to compare these two sealers to determine whether there are differences in pain experienced after treatment and in treatment success, assessed during follow-up visits after 1 and 2 years.
title: Post-operative Pain and Clinical Outcome After Single-cone Obturation With a Calcium Silicate-based Versus Epoxy Resin Sealer

brief_summary:
This study aims to find out whether nurse-led transitional care can help older adults with chronic health conditions recover safely after leaving the hospital. It also examines whether this approach can lower the risk of returning to the hospital within 30 days.

The study includes 652 adults aged 60 years or older with at least one long-term health condition. All participants were receiving care in medical wards at an Italian university hospital and were preparing to return home.

Participants were randomly assigned to one of two groups:

Nurse-led transitional care: Participants received additional care in a nurse-led unit before returning home. Nurses assessed their health and daily needs, provided personalized care and education, and helped plan a safe return home. This approach followed the Fundamentals of Care Framework, which focuses on meeting people's physical, emotional, and social care needs.

Usual care: Participants received standard hospital care and returned directly home after discharge, without the additional nurse-led transitional care program.

Researchers assessed participants' ability to perform daily activities, memory and thinking skills, risk of falls, and risk of developing pressure injuries (skin damage caused by prolonged pressure). They also checked whether participants returned to the hospital unexpectedly within 30 days.

By comparing the two groups, the study aims to understand whether additional nurse-led care can support recovery, improve independence, and help older adults remain safely at home after hospitalization.
title: Effectiveness of a Nurse-Led Transitional Care Model Based on the Fundamentals of Care Framework

brief_summary:
45% of cancer deaths are linked to modifiable factors (behavioral, metabolic). Li-Fraumeni syndrome (LFS), caused by germline TP53 mutations, leads to an extremely high, early-onset cancer risk (≈24× higher than general population).

Current surveillance programs are intensive but show no clear survival benefit; primary prevention is minimal.

Evidence suggests health behaviors (smoking, alcohol, diet, weight, physical activity) may influence cancer risk in TP53 carriers.

Early studies show frequent modifiable risk factors in this population (smoking, overweight/obesity, poor diet).

A major unmet need appears: current LFS care is currently focused almost solely on screening, without any other prevention measures.

This study aims to evaluate this participatory, multidimensional prevention program for germline TP53 carriers. If effective, it could be scaled nationally and internationally
conditions: Adult Carriers of a Pathogenic or Probably Pathogenic (Class 4 and 5) Germline Variation in the TP53 Gene
lead_sponsor: Gustave Roussy, Cancer Campus, Grand Paris
primary_outcomes: Change in the composite Lifestyle Index at 1 year
title: Reduce All Avoidable Cancer-promoting Exposures in Individuals at High Genetic Risk of Cancer Carrying a Constitutional Variant of the TP53 Gene

brief_summary:
This is a Phase I, open-label, multi-center study to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics (PK), and preliminary efficacy of CG-7321 capsules as monotherapy or in combination with fulvestrant in subjects with advanced solid tumors.

The study consists of:

* Part Ia (Monotherapy): Dose escalation (accelerated titration followed by 3+3 design) from 2mg to 50mg twice daily (BID), plus dose expansion cohorts in advanced solid tumors including HR+/HER2- breast cancer, ovarian cancer, gastric cancer, and other tumor types.
* Part Ib (Combination Therapy): Dose escalation of CG-7321 combined with fulvestrant in HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer.
lead_sponsor: Chengdu Cynogen Bio-pharmaceutical Tech. Co., Ltd.
title: A Phase I Study of CG-7321 Monotherapy or Combination Therapy in Advanced Solid Tumors

brief_summary:
Musician's Focal Dystonia (MFD) is a task-specific movement disorder that impairs fine motor control during musical performance and may severely affect professional and amateur musicians. The Modified Integrated Sensorimotor Approach (MISA) is a standardized home-based rehabilitation program that combines mirror therapy, sensory reorganization exercises, graded motor training, and motor awareness strategies to promote sensorimotor retraining.

This retrospective observational study aims to evaluate the association between participation in the MISA rehabilitation program and changes in musical performance among musicians with focal hand dystonia. Musical performance is assessed using the Technical Ability and Performing Scale (TAPS), a patient-reported outcome measure specifically developed for musicians with focal dystonia. Secondary objectives include the investigation of clinical and individual factors potentially associated with treatment response.

The study consists of a review of clinical records of patients who completed the MISA program as part of routine clinical care at the Sol Diesis Outpatient Clinic, IRCCS Fondazione Don Carlo Gnocchi, Milan, Italy.
primary_outcomes: Change in Technical Ability (TA) score of the Technical Ability and Performing Scale (TAPS)
title: Protocol in Musician's Focal Dystonia (MISA)

brief_summary: This single-arm pilot study evaluates the feasibility of nightly wearable monitoring with a ring-type sleep monitor during a 4-week home-based program of submental transcutaneous neuromuscular electrical stimulation in adults with obstructive sleep apnea, and describes changes in the ring-derived apnea-hypopnea index, sleep continuity, STOP-Bang score and upper-airway anatomy on CT before and after training.
title: Nightly Wearable Monitoring During Home-Based Submental Electrical Stimulation for Obstructive Sleep Apnea

brief_summary:
Acute upper respiratory tract infections are the primary cause of pediatric visits and hospitalizations in young children. Nasal congestion and mucus accumulation often cause discomfort, feeding difficulties, and respiratory distress in infants. Nasal lavage using normal saline solution is widely recommended to clear upper airways; however, there is limited evidence regarding the optimal patient posture during irrigation.

This study aims to determine whether patient position-supine (lying on the back) versus sitting (tilted 10 degrees forward)-improves the effectiveness of nasal cavity clearance in children aged 0 to 2 years.

A randomized, parallel, age-stratified clinical trial will be conducted at Pediatric Emergency Department and in Pediatric Hospitalization at Universitary La Paz hospital. Participants will be pediatric patients with mild-to-moderate upper respiratory symptoms requiring nasal lavage as part of their routine care.
primary_outcomes: Effectiveness of nasal cavity cleaning according to the investigator
title: Influence of Patient Positioning During Nasal Lavage

brief_summary: Ninety percent of cases of LBP are nonspecific, which means they do not have an obvious reason like an infection or tumor. Pain that spreads from the thoracic spine to the gluteal area and upper leg is a common sign. Pain that lasts 12 weeks or more is classified as chronic. Non-specific low back pain (NSLBP) is marked by limits in facet joints, increased myofascial thickness, and lower lumbar flexibility, which can lead to further dysfunction. 3D-MFR works on fascia in three planes (sagittal, frontal, and transverse) to remove multidirectional limitations, mostly guided by the therapist. In contrast, DMFR is an active method that combines fascial release and joint mobilization, requiring the therapist to perform movements while the patient continually breathes in a synchronized pattern throughout therapy. While the therapeutic effects of MFR have been extensively studied, but dynamic technique - that is MFR in conjunction with joint mobilization and 3 dimensional myofascial release - that is fascia movements in three plane (sagittal, frontal and transverse) have received less attention. This two-arm randomized controlled trial will compare 3 dimensional and dynamic myofascial release in adults aged 20 to 40 years with CNSLBP. Participants will randomly allocated into two groups. Group A will receive 3 Dimensional myofascial release while group B will receive Dynamic myofascial release. Both groups also receive lumbar mobilization and exercise therapy program as the standard protocol for three sessions/week over four weeks. Outcomes will include pain intensity (NPRS), range of motion (Goniometer) and functional disability (ODI).
primary_outcomes: Pain intensity on Numeric Pain Rating Scale (NPRS)
title: Effects of 3-dimensional Versus Dynamic Myofascial Release Techniques With Lumbar Mobilization and Exercise Therapy Program in Chronic Non-specific Low Back Pain.

brief_summary:
This pilot study will look at whether trenibotulinumtoxinE can shorten or reverse the effect of onabotulinumtoxinA in people being treated for lateral canthal lines (also called crow's feet). OnabotulinumtoxinA is a commonly used treatment that relaxes the muscles around the eyes and smooths these lines, and its effect usually lasts about three to four months. Some people may want the effect to wear off sooner. This study will test whether giving trenibotulinumtoxinE after onabotulinumtoxinA changes how long the effect lasts.

Participants will receive onabotulinumtoxinA on both sides of the face. Using a split-face design, one side of each person's face will then be randomly assigned to receive trenibotulinumtoxinE and the other side will receive a placebo. This lets each person act as their own comparison. \[Number\] adults will take part, and they will be followed for \[length of follow-up\] to see how long the effect on each side of the face lasts. The main measure is \[primary outcome, e.g., time until lateral canthal line severity returns to baseline on each side\]. Safety and side effects will also be recorded.
primary_outcomes: Duration of OnabotulinumtoxinA Effect on Lateral Canthal Lines
title: Can TrenibotulinumtoxinE Reverse OnabotulinumtoxinA Effect in Treating Lateral Canthal Lines?

brief_summary:
This is a Phase 1 clinical study. The purpose of this study is to evaluate the pharmacokinetics, safety and tolerability of ulinastatin for injection after single sequential and multiple continuous intravenous infusions in healthy Chinese volunteers.

Key study questions:

* \- How does ulinastatin behave in the body after single sequential and multiple continuous intravenous infusions?
* \- What are the safety outcomes and side effects in healthy people receiving this investigational drug?
* Study participants will:
* \- Complete screening assessments to check if they meet the study requirements.
* \- Receive either ulinastatin for injection or placebo (inactive substance with no study drug) via intravenous drip.
* \- Follow the study schedule for single sequential infusions and multiple continuous infusions.
* \- Provide blood samples to measure drug concentration in the body.
* \- Undergo safety evaluations including physical examinations, vital sign monitoring and laboratory tests throughout the study period.
* The study will compare data from participants receiving the study drug versus those receiving placebo to assess drug-related exposure and adverse reactions.
primary_outcomes: Area under the plasma concentration-time curve from time zero to the last quantifiable
Area under the plasma concentration-time curve from time zero to infinity (AUC0-inf)
Time to reach peak plasma concentration (Tmax)
Peak plasma concentration at steady state (Cmax,ss)
Trough plasma concentration at steady state (Cmin,ss)
Time to reach peak plasma concentration at steady state (Tmax,ss)
Area under the plasma concentration-time curve during a dosing interval at steady state (AUC0-tau,ss)
Accumulation ratio based on Cmax and AUC0-tau (Rac)
title: Pharmacokinetics, Safety and Tolerability of Single Sequential and Multiple Intravenous Infusions of Ulinastatin for Injection in Healthy Chinese Participants

brief_summary:
This randomized controlled trial will evaluate the effects of a virtual reality (VR) multidomain intervention on cognitive function in older adults with cognitive frailty and explore its underlying mechanisms.

Participants will receive either supervised VR training twice weekly for 8 weeks or multidomain health education. The VR program combines cognitive training, physical exercise, nutrition education, and emotional support.

Cognitive function, physical function, emotional symptoms, and nutritional status will be assessed at baseline and Week 8. Functional near-infrared spectroscopy will assess brain activity to explore potential mechanisms. Intervention feasibility, acceptability, and safety will also be evaluated.
title: Virtual Reality Multidomain Training for Older Adults With Cognitive Frailty
